articles.title: Former Chargers RB Austin Ekeler works out for NFC team
articles.summary: Former Chargers running back Austin Ekeler worked out for the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body:
Former Chargers running back Austin Ekeler worked out for the Panthers on Wednesday.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz shared the news via X.

Ekeler will have a shot at joining a team in 2026 after not signing with a club before the season began.

The Panthers desperately need depth after placing Jonathan Brooks on injured reserve following surgery for a core/groin injury.

Brooks is expected to miss at least six weeks. After Brooks, the Panthers have Chuba Hubbard , who is the clear RB1 and AJ Dillon , who has eight rushing attempts for 25 yards through the first two games.

Ekeler could certainly boost the Panthers' running game. The 31-year-old is known for his versatility and dual-threat ability.

With the Chargers , Ekeler led the NFL in scrimmage touchdowns in 2021 (20 total) and 2022 (18 total).

Ekeler spent his first seven seasons with the Chargers. He played the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Commanders.

articles.title: Davante Adams Shows Off Unlimited Taco Bell Card in Video, Reveals He's 1 of 2 People Who Have It
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams recently showcased his Taco Bell purple card, which lets him eat for free at the fast-food restaurant chain whenever he wants.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams recently showcased his Taco Bell purple card, which lets him eat for free at the fast-food restaurant chain whenever he wants.

"It's got my name, so if anybody tries to rob me you'll never be able to use it," Adams said during a Tuesday appearance on the Up & Adams show (1:12 mark). "It's like a credit card. This purple card is basically like a black card, but it only can be used at Taco Bell. But, it is unlimited. I can get in there and go buy $7 million worth of Taco Bell today if I wanted and go have a Taco Bell party."

"The black card and all that stuff's cool, but a lot of people have that," he added. "Only two people have the purple card right now."

While black cards are extremely exclusive credit cards that are usually invite-only, Adams seems to value his purple card much more.

Actor and comedian Kevin Hart is the only other person known to have a purple card (h/t Awful Announcing's Matt Yoder ).

Adams has been partnered with Taco Bell for years, initially appearing in commercials for the chain in 2022.

The six-time Pro Bowler has opened his 2026 season on a high note, hauling in 11 receptions for 221 yards and two touchdowns through two games.

Adams particularly thrived during the Rams' 28-6 win over the New York Giants in Week 2, catching eight passes for 195 yards and two scores.

articles.title: John Harbaugh doesn't rule out Giants trading for QB, but he might not like what's out there
articles.summary: The pool of unemployed quarterbacks capable of potentially being a starter is shallow enough. The trade pool appears even less deep.
articles.body:
The New York Giants have to rewrite their 2026 plan at quarterback. They're apparently open to any and all avenues for adding another one after starter Jaxson Dart 's season-ending knee surgery .

"We plan on [adding another QB], absolutely," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Wednesday. "Can't say who at this point. We're working on that."

Asked if that included possibly trading for a quarterback, Harbaugh said: "All options are open."

That means the phone lines are open. But Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen might not like what they hear on the other end.

Harbaugh also said he preferred a "veteran" quarterback, which presumably takes trading for a rookie off the table. Without knowing Harbaugh's defintion of "veteran," it seems fair to presume he means someone older and wiser.

Here's the bigger point: Harbaugh might not be able to be very picky right now. The pool of unemployed quarterbacks capable of potentially being a starter is shallow enough. The trade pool might not be deep enough to get your feet wet before they start thinning it out even more.

Why a trade feels unlikely, even with one tantalizing name

What the Giants saw out of Jameis Winston against the Rams was tough enough. He struggled, and it's part of the greater impetus to go get some help and possibly salvage the season. Keep that in mind when you consider that Winston is among the five best-paid backups in the league.

Who else are they going to get? Who's good enough to trade for but not good enough to start for his own team?

Quality backups are hard to find. The 49ers went 5-3 with Mac Jones after Brock Purdy got hurt, even beating the Rams in Los Angeles . The Texans went 3-0 with Davis Mills replacing an injured C.J. Stroud . Both of those teams made the playoffs. They'd have regretted giving away players who helped them get there.

That's why Jones might be untouchable, even if they're going to lose him in free agency. Better to get the compensatory-pick value later if the 49ers view themselves as contenders. The same might apply to Mills, the Saints' Spencer Rattler , or even the Vikings' Carson Wentz (don't worry, we'll get to the other guy).

The Colts' Anthony Richardson Sr. is a name you'll hear, but why? He'd be an interesting reclamation project, but Richardson hasn't played much in two years and might not be the "veteran" Harbaugh is thinking of. He's viewed more as a developmental piece than a plug-and-play option, even if his running skills could help uplift an offense.

The Raiders aren't trading Kirk Cousins at 2-0; they're still using him. And who's trading for any of the Falcons' QBs? No one. Could the Steelers decide to offload Mason Rudolph ? Sure. But giving up much for him feels foolish. Same goes for Gardner Minshew and others of that ilk. Though Harbaugh has a past with Tyler Huntley , the Baltimore backup probably isn't available.

That's why signing a street veteran feels more likely, such as Brandon Allen (who has strong connections with Giants QB coach Brian Callahan), Jimmy Garoppolo or even Josh Johnson , the ultimate hired gun when your starter goes down. That guy has been in every offensive system imaginable, once even playing college football for Jim Harbaugh almost 20 years ago.

Sign a guy, and if he stinks, you move on. You're already in the hole. No point in trading for someone who might not be great either.

The one name that might make sense, but buyer beware

Yes, there will be some who float the J.J. McCarthy idea, and it certainly can't be immediately waved away. It's admittedly the most interesting of the trade options, although there are reasons not to do it, too.

You can connect almost as many dots as you want there. The obvious need for a restart for McCarthy, who was a national champion in college not that long ago. The clear Harbaugh connection. The Giants brought McCarthy in for a pre-draft visit (before Harbaugh was there) and supposedly liked him.

The question is how much the Giants still like McCarthy now. And how much they could envision a player with 10 NFL starts — and passing numbers similar to Richardson — helping steady their team this season. There's still a long-term vision to think about here, but the Giants also need to win now, or there could be more changes.

The Vikings badly wanted McCarthy to take the job and run with it, and they couldn't in good conscience do it and live with the results they thought they'd get from him. Wentz might not have been part of the Vikings' starting competition, but he was the one to replace Kyler Murray (and lead them to a 2-0 start), not McCarthy.

There might be some sense in having McCarthy behind Winston and try to mold him as competition or insurance for Dart. But the idea of giving up anything significant for the Giants, who are already missing their 2027 fourth-round draft pick, is a tough one to embrace.

Giants fans might want to prepare themselves to not be underwhelmed when they consider the options to replace Dart, especially when it comes to a trade.

articles.title: When The Coach Asks The Questions: Marcus Freeman Interviews Jadarian Price
articles.summary: Here is Marcus Freeman’s one-on-one interview with Jadarian Price.
articles.body: When Jadarian Price first stepped onto Notre Dame’s campus, he couldn't have predicted the impact he would make in South Bend. Even in a shared backfield under head coach Marcus Freeman, Price became half of a dynamic backfield duo alongside Jeremiyah Love. Fast forward two years, and both Price and Love heard their names called in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Love went third overall to the Arizona Cardinals, while Price closed out Day 1 at Pick 32, landing with the Seattle Seahawks. Through two weeks of the season, Price is already making his mark in Seattle after taking over following Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker's free agent departure for the Kansas City Chiefs. Price has rushed for 104 yards and 4.5 yards per carry, taking control of the backfield. How’s his former coach Marcus Freeman doing? He has the Fighting Irish sitting at 3-0 and ranked No. 3 in the latest AP Poll. Even after losing Love and Price to the NFL Draft, Freeman still has this offense humming. When Freeman and Price finally got the chance to catch up, the dynamic had shifted. This time, Freeman sat down with Price for an interview to hear about his NFL journey so far and what life has been like since leaving South Bend. Here is Freeman’s one-on-one interview with Price: Did Price Stiff-Arm Or Truck A Cardinals Defender? Price's Response: "I trucked somebody. It helps to have a good offensive line and the past two games they’ve knocked guys off the ball. They’re getting past the line of scrimmage pretty good and these guys are legit, but I’m trusting my talent." The Biggest Different Between Seattle And South Bend? Price's Response: "Seattle in some ways is a lot like South Bend. It’s starting to get a little gloomy now, but that’s football weather. The program values spiritual life and all that stuff here. People have bible study here. A good majority of guys do chapel and mass the night before the game." What Was It Like Seeing Eli Raridon Score? Price's Response: "I didn’t realize that he was the one who scored until after the game. He was the first person to score in the NFL because that was the first game of the season. Like that’s legit and pretty cool, man. It was good talking to him after the game." How's Julian Love And Ex-Notre Dame Players Doing? Price's Response: "They’re doing great, and I think they’re getting awards every week. We do team awards and Julian Love had a pick in like every game. He’s always around the ball. Riley [Mills] has been getting tackles for loss and things like that. But yeah, they're a great part of our team, and we did Notre Dame events with them back in the off season in the summer, all three of us." On Joe Montana Reaching Out Price's Response: "Montana reached out…Joe Montana. For this like a venture capital thing. So we spoke to this tech company startup. We were just talking to them about connecting football to the life of a CEO or something like that. It was pretty cool." Jeremiyah Love Jersey Swap After Week 2 Matchup? Price's Response: "Yeah. We didn’t get to do the jersey swap this time but luckily we play them [The Cardinals] twice. I think we’ll do a jersey swap next time."

articles.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur backs Marvin Harrison Jr as viral videos fuel questions about receiver's effort
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. has just one catch through two games as clips questioning his effort fuel criticism of the Arizona Cardinals' third-year wideout.
articles.body: The Arizona Cardinals’ season-opening victory over the Los Angeles Chargers was quickly overshadowed in Week 2, when they fell 31-7 to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 2. Much of the postgame conversation centered on wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., who finished without a catch as Arizona’s offense struggled to find a rhythm. Last Sunday’s performance was the latest sign of a relatively quiet start to the 2026 season for the third-year receiver and No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Harrison entered the league widely regarded as one of the top receiving prospects in recent memory, but he has managed just one reception for 33 yards through two games. He has yet to establish himself as a consistent part of the Cardinals’ passing game. The concerns about Harrison’s development are not new. Injury setbacks limited him to 12 games last season, when he finished with 604 receiving yards and four touchdowns. The former Ohio State standout is still searching for his first 1,000-yard NFL season, and his slow start this year has only amplified the criticism surrounding him. 2026 NFL OROY ODDS: LOVE FAVORED; BOSTON RISES AFTER BIG WEEK 2 The scrutiny surrounding Harrison has recently extended beyond his production. Clips highlighting his route running and blocking have prompted some observers to question what they perceive as a lack of effort during games. LaFleur pushed back on the criticism, arguing that Harrison’s running style should not be interpreted as a lack of effort. "I don’t see it that way," LaFleur said. "I think his running style is different than some other people’s, I would say that. If that’s people’s narrative on him, that’s fine. I know his teammates don’t feel that way." Harrison’s tape has shown flashes of the precise route running and polished technique that helped establish him as largely a "can’t-miss" prospect. At other times, however, he has appeared frustrated while dealing with drops or falling short of his own standards. THREE WORD GAME: THREE WORDS TO DESCRIBE EVERY NFL TEAM SO FAR THIS SEASON AHEAD OF WEEK 3 Even as Harrison has struggled to find his footing, other players in Arizona’s offense have flourished. Tight end Trey McBride earned first-team All-Pro honors last season and emerged as one of the top players at his position. Wide receiver Michael Wilson surpassed the 1,000-yard mark in 2025 and was rewarded with a contract extension this offseason. About halfway through last season, Hall of Fame receiver Marvin Harrison Sr. criticized the Cardinals’ offense, saying it was difficult to watch his son’s team play. Arizona has since made changes to its offensive coaching staff and scheme, but those adjustments have yet to translate into improved production for Harrison. LaFleur acknowledged Harrison’s slow start but stressed that the Cardinals must balance his involvement with the needs of the offense. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I know it’s just ‘get some easy completions and get going,’" the first-year Cardinals coach noted. "You also have Trey McBride, who’s one of the best underneath guys in the world and there’s only about 60 to 65 plays a game. And you’ve got to run the ball. You’ve got Kendrick [Bourne], who works underneath pretty well, too. Everyone’s kind of got their role right there."

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. Reacts to Criticism Amid Struggles to Start 2026 NFL Season with Cardinals
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. discussed his reaction to criticism of his slow start to the 2026 season on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. discussed his reaction to criticism of his slow start to the 2026 season on Wednesday.

"It's a social media era, you see everything," Harrison told reporters. "I'm not going to sit here and say I don't see nothing. You get told to block out the noise and not pay attention to it. That's part of it, you can still see something and still block it out. I see everything, and everybody's entitled to their own opinions. You get platforms to speak your mind and that's okay for me. I'm just gonna continue to worry about my team and my process and helping the team win best I can."

The 24-year-old also confirmed that he isn't going to let outside noise impact his approach.

"Stick to my process," Harrison said. "Don't change anything I've been doing. Continue to work hard day in and day out. That's the best you can do in this situation."

Expectations were high for Harrison after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft.

He appeared in 17 games as a rookie, hauling in 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns.

While Harrison only racked up 608 receiving yards and four touchdowns during his second season in 2025, it's worth noting that he missed five games due to injuries .

He's struggled to make an impact to open his 2026 campaign, though.

In two appearances this year, Harrison has caught just one of his four targets for 33 yards. He's also recorded one drop.

Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett owns an 86.2 passer rating in 2026, which drops to 61.5 when targeting Harrison (via Pro Football Focus ).

Arizona owns a 1-1 record, but the team has scored just 33 points in two contests.

As Harrison looks to get back on track, he isn't focused on criticism surrounding his beginning of the year.

articles.title: Commanders Players Call Out 'Bulls--t' Jayden Daniels Narrative After Viral Video of QB's Injury
articles.summary: Washington Commanders players were seen walking away from quarterback Jayden Daniels after he suffered a dislocated left elbow at the end of the first half of their 37-20 road loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders players were seen walking away from quarterback Jayden Daniels after he suffered a dislocated left elbow at the end of the first half of their 37-20 road loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

Some fans online questioned how those images looked. However, the video doesn't tell the whole story, per Commanders players who loudly denied the accusations.

"It's bulls--t what people are saying," left tackle Brandon Coleman said, per ESPN's John Keim , who relayed player comments on Wednesday. "Jay's our guy and he's been our guy. There's no malice behind it."

Offensive tackle Josh Conerly Jr. had this to say, via Keim.

"I definitely felt some type of way about it. For people to say we don't care it kind of hurts because there's a lot of care. But I don't care what anyone says on the outside. We all care for our quarterback and we're all behind him on that moment. You can't go off a simple 10-second clip."

Additonal context regarding the timing of the injury deserves mention. JP Finlay of NBC Sports Washington provided it, noting that Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told his team to head to the locker room for halftime.

Halftime began, and the clock was ticking towards the third quarter. There was obviously a difficult and emotional situation on the field occurring, but the players somehow had to stomach a difficult situation, absorb what happened and somehow get ready for the second half at the same time.

"It's just the opposite of that. These guys were absolutely gutted," Quinn said.

"When the half is over, the referees are saying, 'Man, I can't delay the half. They can't stay on the field.' The players were like, 'No, we want to stay.'

"So it's just the opposite of that. They were gutted. They love this guy. So halftime was hard and emotional in that space."

As tight end Ben Sinnott noted, it was a "weird situation."

"All that stuff is ridiculous," Sinnott said. "As far as the love and brotherhood we have for Jayden, it's really strong. We've seen how hard he worked to get to where he's been.

"It was a weird situation, people were trying to figure out what's going on and they wanted to give the trainers space to do it. You don't want to crowd the guy. Obviously guys are taking a step back and giving him space, praying, and we all came back.

For further proof on that being the case, last November, Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow against the Seattle Seahawks in the fourth quarter near the Seattle goal line as his team searched for a touchdown. His teammates surrounded him en masse then as he walked off the field in pain.

In the present date, there is no official timeline for Daniels' return to the field. Marcus Mariota replaced Daniels in the second half at Dallas, and he'll start on Sunday, when Washington hosts the Seahawks at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Bills’ Landon Jackson Already Faces Second NFL Punishment of 2026
articles.summary: Bills edge rusher Landon Jackson faces his second NFL punishment of 2026, adding another disciplinary issue for the Buffalo defender. The post Bills’ Landon...
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills defensive end Landon Jackson now awaits an NFL punishment for tripping Jahmyr Gibbs , and a preseason strike already sits on his record.

The league's second-offense rate for tripping runs $18,507, and nobody outside the NFL office knows yet whether the second-year pass rusher will be billed as a repeat violator.

The foul came with six seconds left before halftime of Buffalo 's 41-31 Thursday night win over the Detroit Lions on Sept. 17. Jared Goff handed off to Gibbs, who churned 7 yards to the Buffalo 33 before Jackson made the stop, according to EssentiallySports.

Bills ' Landon Jackson Awaits Fine Decision

Officials saw a trip, not a tackle. The flag tacked on 13 yards, though the Bills already held a 27-10 cushion and the clock had all but expired. The on-field cost was minor. The financial one is still pending.

The NFL's 2026 fine schedule sets the striking, kicking, tripping and kneeing category at $12,537 for a first violation and $18,507 for a second. Neither figure is automatic. League officials must first rule the play fine-worthy, then slot it into a category.

Tripping also falls outside the three-strike system that can trigger suspensions for hip-drop tackles, horse-collars, launching, hits on defenseless players and blindside blocks. Jackson's exposure is financial. A suspension is not on the table.

The NFL's officiating department screens every snap from every game and forwards possible violations to Football Operations for a closer look. A flag thrown on the field simply guarantees the play lands on that desk.

Bills' Jackson Awaits Ruling Before Chargers Game

Jackson already owns a line in the league's discipline ledger. The NFL docked him $8,190 for an unnecessary roughness foul in that same category during the second quarter of Buffalo's preseason opener against the Carolina Panthers , according to SI.com . Only two players league-wide drew bigger preseason fines.

The league discounts preseason discipline, with no game checks yet on the table. Even so, Cleveland Browns lineman Tytus Howard absorbed $12,537 for an August tripping foul, according to Pro Football Talk .

Any player who contests a fine gets a hearing before an appeals officer selected jointly by the league and the players union, according to Pro Football Talk . This season's panel includes Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson and James Thrash.

Regular-season discipline drops on the Saturday after each week of games. That puts Jackson's verdict on Sept. 26, one day before Buffalo hosts the Los Angeles Chargers .

Buffalo drafted Jackson 72nd overall in 2025 out of Arkansas, using a pick acquired from Chicago . He appeared in three games as a rookie before MCL and PCL damage against the Miami Dolphins in Week 10 ended his season.

Jackson piled up 16 sacks across three seasons with the Razorbacks and earned first-team All-SEC honors from the conference's coaches in 2023. Through two games this fall, he has three tackles and no sacks.

Gibbs knows the league's accounting office too. The Lions running back was fined $23,027 for lowering his helmet on a Week 1 touchdown against the New Orleans Saints , a play that drew no flag, according to NFL Network 's Mike Garafolo . That hit stood as the costliest fine of the opening week .

articles.title: Minnesota Vikings Star Justin Jefferson Gets Honest About Kyler Murray’s Return
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have gone 2-0 to begin the 2026 NFL season. After pulling off a shocking comeback win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, they took c...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have gone 2-0 to begin the 2026 NFL season. After pulling off a shocking comeback win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, they took care of business against the Chicago Bears in Week 2.

Last week, the Vikings were able to defeat the Bears by a final score of 9-3. Carson Wentz started the game after Kyler Murray was ruled out due to the concussion he suffered against the Packers. In Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Murray is set to resume the starting role.

Murray was signed to a one-year deal during the NFL offseason after he was released by the Arizona Cardinals . He beat out J.J. McCarthy for the starting job during training camp and preseason action. The hope was that Murray would be able to help Justin Jefferson get back on track.

So far this season, fans haven't gotten a true look at the connection between Murray and Jefferson.

Ahead of this week's game against the Buccaneers, Jefferson was asked for his thoughts about Murray's return. He was happy to offer an answer.

Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson Speaks About Kyler Murray's Return

During a media session on Wednesday, Jefferson made his thoughts crystal clear about Murray being his starting quarterback.

"Looking forward to it," Jefferson said . "Obviously, what we've built throughout training camp, throughout the offseason, leading into the season, has definitely been exciting and something that we've all been waiting for. The time was limited the first game. So, for him to be back out there and for us to get started with him is going to be a joy to see."

In Week 1, Murray didn't play very long before the concussion occurred. He completed three of his five pass attempts for 18 yards and an interception. Needless to say, it wasn't the best debut for the former No. 1 overall pick from the 2019 NFL Draft.

Throughout his career, Murray has shown flashes of star potential. He has played in 88 career games, completing 67.1 percent of his pass attempts for 20,478 yards, 121 touchdowns, and 61 interceptions, while also running for 3,202 yards and 32 touchdowns.

At 29 years old, there is still a chance that Murray could be a long-term option for the Vikings. Minnesota can only hope that he can be an option past the 2026 season.

Only time will tell what the rest of the season has in store. That being said, the Vikings are going to get their first real look at the Murray-Jefferson connection this week against Tampa Bay . Jefferson sounds excited about it.

articles.title: In 2022, Miami Dolphins star Zach Sieler and his wife launched an outdoor foundation; four years later, their 250-acre Missouri property is becoming a farm and conservation classroom for children
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle and team captain Zach Sieler and his wife Hannah are developing their 250-acre property in Missouri into a place where
articles.body: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle and team captain Zach Sieler and his wife Hannah are developing their 250-acre property in Missouri into a place where children can learn about agriculture, conservation and the outdoors. The couple launched the Sieler Safe Haven Foundation as a non-profit in 2022, after an experience at their hunting camp led them to create more opportunities for young people to experience nature.Sieler spoke about the plans during his appearance on the Like A Farmer podcast, where he discussed football, fatherhood, farming, hunting and his family’s life outdoors. The episode also covers his plans to begin raising cattle on the Missouri property.The property is now part of the foundation’s work with children. The Sieler Safe Haven Foundation describes its Missouri site as a “hands-on learning laboratory where agriculture meets adventure”. Its programmes include experiences related to farming, wildlife, land management, fishing and hunting.The foundation’s work grew from an experience in 2019, when Zach and Hannah welcomed a young man who uses a wheelchair to their hunting camp. They realised that traditional hunting was not accessible to him and began thinking about how outdoor experiences could be made available to more young people. Three years later, they officially registered the foundation as a non-profit.Building outdoor lessonsThe Sielers say their own experiences outdoors shaped their interest in creating such opportunities for children. Zach grew up in Pinckney, Michigan, where his father introduced him to hunting, fishing and outdoor activities on their 30-acre property.Hannah Sieler, who is from Ozark, Missouri, also had an active childhood, although she had limited experience camping in tents with her family. According to the foundation, her understanding of what young people can miss without exposure to the outdoors has influenced her work with the organisation.The foundation now runs programmes that combine outdoor education with activities such as agriculture, wildlife management, fishing, hunting and sports. It says these experiences are intended to help young people develop practical skills, confidence and an understanding of environmental stewardship.The foundation says participants can take part in turkey and whitetail deer hunts, fishing and activities involving wildlife and land management. The property also works with the Land Legacy Partnership on a plan for managing wildlife on the property.Plans for farming and conservationSieler told Like A Farmer that his family plans to begin raising cattle in Missouri. The foundation also says land management is also part of its work in Missouri. Its partnership with the Land Legacy Partnership includes practices such as controlled burns, timber improvements and natural farming methods.The aim is not only to provide outdoor activities but also to teach young people about the land and how it is managed. The foundation describes these experiences as opportunities to understand land stewardship and sustainable living practices.Reaching more childrenThe Missouri property is one part of the Sieler Safe Haven Foundation’s work. The organisation also runs programmes in Florida and Michigan and helps facilitate educational trips in other locations.In Florida, its programmes focus on fishing, wetland conservation, wildlife management and cultural enrichment. In Michigan, it offers programmes involving forest management, wildlife conservation and outdoor recreation.The foundation also organises other activities for children. articles.title: Antonio Brown: Ex-NFL wide receiver to avoid prison with reduced charge in attempted murder case
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers, New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Antonio Brown could have faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original attempted murder charge.
articles.body:
His lawyer said on Wednesday the agreement with prosecutors was too good to turn down.

Brown is scheduled to appear in court on September 30 to make the deal final. Defense attorney Mark Eiglarsh said Brown will plead no contest to aggravated assault. He will be sentenced to probation, and adjudication will be withheld, meaning Brown will not be considered a convicted felon, the attorney said.

Brown could have faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original attempted murder charge.

Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a security staffer after a celebrity boxing match in Miami on May 16, 2025, and firing two shots at a man he had gotten into a fistfight with earlier, according to an arrest warrant. Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told investigators that one of the bullets grazed his neck.

Attorney insists that Brown would have prevailed at trial.

"This was not an easy decision," Eiglarsh said in a statement Wednesday. "Antonio believes in his innocence. He believes strongly in his Stand Your Ground defense, and he believes he would ultimately prevail at trial. But when prosecutors put an offer on the table that transforms a potential decades-long prison sentence into a significantly reduced charge and probation, there was simply no way he could reasonably turn it down."

Florida's so-called Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Richard Cooper, an attorney for Nantambu, called the plea deal fair.

"We are satisfied that justice is served. My client maintains what he said previously: that he forgives Brown and will not cooperate with law enforcement," Cooper said in an email Wednesday. "We wish Mr. Brown good health and that he grows from this event."

In a previous statement, Nantambu's attorneys said he had made the decision to forgive Brown after "considerable reflection, prayer, and consultation with his family and counsel."

Brown has said on social media that he was defending himself from an attack and that others were trying to steal jewelry from him.

Brown, 38, spent 12 years in the NFL and was an All-Pro wide receiver who last played in 2021 for Tampa Bay, including winning a Super Bowl championship with quarterback Tom Brady. He spent much of his career with Pittsburgh. For his career, Brown had 928 receptions for more than 12,000 yards and accounted for 88 total touchdowns, counting punt returns and one pass.

Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June 2025.

He previously had been accused of battery of a moving truck driver, several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents. During a 2021 game with Tampa Bay against the New York Jets , Brown took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field, leading to his release by the Buccaneers and effectively ending his football career.

In a separate case, Nantambu was found guilty earlier this year of a misdemeanour charge of resisting an officer after police said he disrupted Kendrick Lamar's Super Bowl half-time performance in 2025.

Nantambu was among dozens of dancers on the field at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans when he ran across the field with a Sudanese flag that read "Sudan and Free Gaza." He surrendered to authorities after an arrest warrant was obtained.

articles.title: Commanders push back on 'bulls—' viral narrative that they didn't care about Jayden Daniels' elbow injury
articles.summary: Dan Quinn says Commanders players were "gutted" after Jayden Daniels' elbow injury, pushing back on viral video showing teammates walking away.
articles.body: You think you saw what happened after Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow last Sunday, and it was troubling. The Washington Commanders quarterback was on the turf, writhing in pain, and his teammates seemed to simply ignore him. Most simply walked off the field. And it seemed to send the message that they didn't care. COMMANDERS FACE CRITICAL DECISION ON JAYDEN DANIELS' ELBOW AS SPECIALISTS REVIEW MRI RESULTS The Commanders have gotten crushed on social media for the video of players walking away – because it was jarring compared to New York Giants or Green Bay Packers players huddling around teammates when they went down. It suggested Daniels isn't beloved or even respected by teammates. "I'm glad you brought that up because it's just the opposite in fact," coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday. "These guys were absolutely gutted." Quinn said the timing of the injury happening on the final play of the first half and signaling the start of halftime played a major role in the walk-off. "When the half was over, the referees even came and said they can't delay the half and we can't stay on the field," Quinn said. "And they were like, ‘No, I'm staying.’ So it's just the opposite in fact. "They were gutted, they love this guy, and so halftime was hard. It was emotional in that space." The perception of the Washington walk-off may have come from television. The live broadcast went to a commercial at halftime. And ESPN's highlights showed Daniels collapsing to the ground as players walked by him, then cut to him leaving on the cart. But all that missed what happened in the stadium. Multiple players, led by backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, indeed came onto the field as trainers attended to Daniels and eventually called for the cart to take him away. Some of them even returned from the locker room to do it. "It’s bull—- what people are saying," left tackle Brandon Coleman told reporters. "Jay’s our guy and he’s been our guy. There’s no malice behind it." The narrative that the Commanders abandoned their quarterback is actually an excellent study on how social media wields the power to shape opinion, that opinion reaches legacy media, and then can reach into an NFL team's facility. Even when the narrative is basically fake news. JAXSON DART TORE HIS MCL AND MENISCUS REQUIRING SURGERY "We all care for our quarterback," offensive lineman Josh Conerly said. "You can’t go off a simple 10-second clip." Mariota takes over for Daniels at quarterback now while the starter and the team continue to figure out what to do about his injury, with options including season-ending surgery. There's nothing positive about the situation for the team. But Quinn made it clear ahead of time that Mariota is respected and he is confident in the new quarterback. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I think the nice part with Marcus, man, he does have a real command on things that we need," Quinn said. "There's a specific way, like in each game, that you have to go about it and what it takes to win. We hit that with the team today. "But with Marcus, he's one that's really in control, has good vision of it, what it is, where to go. You can hear that type of communication with him. So I think, number one, him running the system gives everybody a calmness about them knowing that he’ll take care of it." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 3 2026 NFL Picks and Predictions
articles.summary: If Week 2 in the NFL has taught us anything, it's that we still don't know much about these teams. Also, if everyone on an expert panel agrees, expect the unexpected.
articles.body:
If Week 2 in the NFL has taught us anything, it's that we still don't know much about these teams. Also, if everyone on an expert panel agrees, expect the unexpected.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , were all on the Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. The Eagles failed to cover, and the Buccaneers lost outright.

On the flip side, the group improved to 4-2 on its lone-wolf picks, so make sure to pay attention to the contrarian analysis.

This week, we have four lone-wolf picks and two unanimous ones, which means a lot of agreement across our panel. Though if the brave solo experts are right, we could see early separation in the standings below. Moton leads the group, but his colleagues can make up some ground on the upcoming slate.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 22, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Atlanta Falcons (0-2) at Green Bay Packers (1-1)

To be fair, the Green Bay Packers haven't looked great this year—Green Bay blew a sizable lead in Minnesota and would have lost to the Jets if Gang Green had a head coach who could tell time. But a rusty Michael Penix isn't going to fix the many things that are wrong with the Atlanta Falcons, so this is a (green and) golden opportunity for a get-right game at home. Let the Cheeseheads rejoice.

The only things the Packers should be excited about is that they finally get to play at Lambeau Field after back-to-back road games, and that one of those road games was against the Jets; they're lucky to be 1-1 right now. Green Bay hosts a Falcons team that gets Michael Penix Jr. back from injury a week after scoring only three points against a Panthers defense that surrendered 59 points the week before that.

Whether Penix's return is a good omen remains to be seen, but nonsensical things are happening around the NFL right now — I mean, Christian Watson is on pace to shatter career highs by the halfway point of the season, if he stays healthy, for goodness' sake — which means expect the unexpected. On paper, the Packers should blow the doors off the Falcons, so I'm taking the points.

Packers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski

Carolina Panthers (1-1) at Cleveland Browns (1-1)

The Cleveland Browns are playing their first home game against a Carolina Panthers team playing its second straight road game. It feels strange backing the Browns to cover a tight spread, but Cleveland's defense was solid against Tampa Bay, and I think the Panthers' attack has to come back to Earth at some point, as they've scored at least 34 points in each of their first two games.

The Browns will look to turn this one into an uglier, lower-scoring affair, and I think they make it happen. Cleveland pulls the upset, and we finally get a Jared Verse sighting.

The Panthers are off to a hot start, at least offensively. Bryce Young and Co. are averaging over 400 yards per game through their first two contests. Conversely, the Browns find themselves among the bottom half of the league in total defense. Cleveland's offense surprised with its performance last week. Though that level of play shouldn't be expected. If things go wrong early, the Browns could easily lose home-field advantage thanks to a hostile fanbase.

Panthers: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Los Angeles Chargers (0-2) at Buffalo Bills (2-0)

The Buffalo Bills' offense is unstoppable right now, and I sense Jim Leonhard's aggressive defense is on the verge of a breakout performance. Meanwhile, something still isn't right with the Los Angeles Chargers, who are quite banged up and less rested heading into this tough road game.

It's only Week 3, but the Chargers are on the precipice of a lost season. A third straight defeat would leave L.A. in historically bad company, as fewer than three percent of 0-3 teams have made the postseason since 1990.

While the Houston Texans actually accomplished this feat only a year ago, the AFC West is not the AFC South, and Jim Harbaugh's team looks completely flustered, if not entirely lost, and faces a brutal schedule through mid-November. Next on that schedule is the NFL's hottest team, the Bills, and current, overwhelming MVP front-runner Josh Allen ( +185 at FanDuel ). Are you for real, Justin Herbert? Last chance to prove it.

Bills: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Tennessee Titans (0-2) at New York Giants (1-1)

The Tennessee Titans came close to upsetting the Eagles in Week 2, but I think that game says more about Philadelphia than it does about Tennessee. While I could see the Titans coming into New York and beating a Jaxson Dart-less Giants team, I don't think it'll actually happen.

I'm just not convinced we'll see Robert Saleh's squad put together back-to-back good games, and I don't think the Giants will hamper themselves quite like the Eagles did. While New York's offense didn't look good with Jameis Winston behind center on Monday night, we should see John Harbaugh adapt and bring a different approach with a week to prepare.

Rock meets hard place. The Giants experienced what may wind up being the biggest high-to-low of any team this entire season, and they did it in only five quarters. On the heels of a huge, emotional division win to open the John Harbaugh era, everything literally came crashing down for New York as Jaxson Dart crashed to the ground on the first drive of Week 2.

Big Blue could rally around that injury in this game, sure, but Jameis Winston's MNF performance makes Giants fans long for the days of Tommy DeVito as the unexpected starting QB. There's no trust in the Titans, either, but taking the points is the safest option here.

Titans: Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Kansas City Chiefs (2-0) at Miami Dolphins (0-2)

The Kansas City Chiefs feel like they're back. Travis Kelce looks like he's turned back the clock. Kenneth Walker III leads a dominant run game. The defense is opportunistic. And they have Patrick Mahomes and a chip on their shoulder after a disappointing 2025 season. The Miami Dolphins have none of these things and are completely overmatched here. I usually hesitate to back heavy favorites, but I don't see this game being close.

A double-digit spread is a lot this early in the process, but there's little reason to doubt whether the Chiefs are deserving of the number upon facing the Dolphins. Miami already lost its first two games by 14 or more points. The Dolphins also feature the league's worst roster. Meanwhile, K.C. once again looks like a major contender. The spread should probably be even larger than it is.

Chiefs: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cincinnati Bengals (2-0) at Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1)

I don't know that I trust the Cincinnati Bengals enough yet to give up a hook in a divisional road game against a veteran opponent that needs the W. Watch for the Pittsburgh Steelers' pass rush to be the difference in a close victory against a Cincinnati team that hasn't started 3-0 in over a decade.

The Steelers offense is a mess. Aaron Rodgers doesn't have it anymore, and Mike McCarthy hasn't had any noticeable impact through two weeks. But the real problem is the offensive line, which has allowed six sacks against a Bengals group that's leading the league with eight so far this year. Rodgers can't avoid pressure anymore, and Cincinnati will generate some.

Pittsburgh's defense has done its job this season, but Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase are a different sort of challenge. This rivalry typically winds up being closer than expected no matter what it looks like on paper, so I'll say the Bengals win by four, but it could be more this time around.

Bengals: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

New England Patriots (1-1) at Jacksonville Jaguars (1-1)

Losing Mike Onwenu is a big blow for the New England Patriots, and I think it could lead to serious issues against the Jacksonville Jaguars' pass rush in Jacksonville. However, Mike Vrabel should have a plan for limiting the miscues after watching Drake Maye throw four interceptions in his first two games.

I'm less certain that Trevor Lawrence and the Jags will hold it together after melting down against the Broncos on Sunday. New England has one of the league's top defenses, and if Bo Nix can effectively blast holes in Jacksonville's so-so secondary, so can Maye.

Expect the Jaguars to bounce back at home after a disappointing loss to the Denver Broncos. Furthermore, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has made too many mistakes early in the season. Granted, Maye has been forced to press some due to A.J. Brown's injury. Comparatively, the Jags' offense fields more firepower to move the ball, even against a top-four defense.

Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Houston Texans (0-2) at Indianapolis Colts (0-2)

Don't hit the panic button on the Houston Texans. They've started the season 0-2 in three of the previous four seasons and made the playoffs with double-digit wins. For whatever reason, under head coach DeMeco Ryans, this team starts slowly and then gains steam as the season goes on.

The Texans won't have Nico Collins, which will make it more difficult for them to flip the switch, but the Indianapolis Colts won't have their most explosive receiver, Alec Pierce.

With two 0-2 squads trying to shake off an early-season funk, take the team that's accustomed to doing it by at least a field goal.

Only two games into the season, the Colts already find themselves in a must-win scenario. Granted, the Texans also own an 0-2 record, but these situations are not the same.

Head coach Shane Steichen and his staff know their jobs are on the line. This team will be desperate for a win at home to prove this season isn't going to spiral out of control like it did last year. The offense is good enough to move the ball, even against the Texans defense. The question is whether Lou Anarumo's defense actually shows up and gets a stop or two. In truth, the unit can't be much worse than it's already been.

Texans: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

New York Jets (1-1) at Detroit Lions (1-1)

The Jets are still inconsistent and need an identity. Whereas the Detroit Lions know who they are: a high-scoring team that has defensive lapses . It's questionable as to whether Gang Green can take advantage of Detroit's defensive shortcomings without a foundational offensive approach.

Plus, the Lions had extra time to make defensive adjustments for a get-right home game. The Jets played two teams with limited/one dimensional offenses. Now, they have the tough task of trying to stop running back Jahmyr Gibbs, wideouts Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams and tight end Sam LaPorta.

Forget the Aaron Glenn revenge narrative here; this may not end well for him. The Jets are averaging 20 points in two games, while the Lions have scored 31 in both of their outings.

The Lions need to get right, but Jets coach Aaron Glenn knows the Lions pretty gorydamn well. New York has punched above its weight two weeks into the season, and this game is ripe for Detroit to make a statement — if it is any sort of legitimate playoff team, which remains to be seen — but I will not ignore an embattled coach returning to his former team and rallying a strong effort.

A 6.5 spread is too big a number for me to lay down right now. Jets cover in either a hard-fought game or silly circumstance.

Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

Seattle Seahawks (2-0) at Washington Commanders (0-2)

Normally, a West Coast team making a cross-country trip to play at 1:00 p.m. Eastern, laying this many points, would be cause for concern. But the Washington Commanders just lost their starting quarterback, while the Seattle Seahawks haven't missed a beat without theirs. Seattle's defense looks like one of the NFL's best (again), while Washington's looks like one of the worst (again). No trap game. No upset. Just carnage.

I'm not sure that this game will be as easy for Seattle as we all seem to expect. I expect that both teams will be playing with backup quarterbacks, and the Seahawks face a daunting cross-country trip and an early start time.

Marcus Mariota is one of the league's better backups, and if he plays well while the Seahawks come out sluggish, I could see Washington keeping this one extremely close. Ultimately, though, I'm not sure the Commanders can keep it close enough to cover without Jayden Daniels.

The Seahawks are better with Sam Darnold in the lineup, but they've been fine with Drew Lock.

Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Arizona Cardinals (1-1) at San Francisco 49ers (2-0)

Ready for the amazing insight into how the Arizona Cardinals are going to keep this close and maybe even win outright? Are you sure you're ready? Absolutely sure? Totally, absolutely sure? 100 percent totally, absolutely sure? Are you sitting down? Ready to have your mind blown? Your world rocked? OK, here goes (hope you're ready)—there is zero chance the Cardinals win in Santa Clara. This call is all about a back-door cover. Like I have insight. Come on, fams.

The San Francisco 49ers are quickly running out of healthy WRs, but San Francisco has looked excellent in each of its first two games with Brock Purdy playing at a high level. The Cardinals lost to a Drew Lock-led Seahawks team in Week 2, so it's hard to see them faring well on the road. Trey McBride is good. The rest of his team is not. 49ers win by double digits.

49ers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Minnesota Vikings (2-0) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2)

The Bucs are now 2-9 in their last 11 games. It's time to accept that this team needs a rebuild. I expect them to struggle mightily against Minnesota's defense and Justin Jefferson in another home loss.

Baker Mayfield needs to get out of the current funk in which he finds himself. Brian Flores' ultra-aggressive defense certainly won't make matters any easier on Tampa Bay's recently re-signed quarterback.

However, Mayfield tends to be at his worst when he's pressing. A week ago, the matchup against the Cleveland Browns was viewed as a revenge game. Clearly, the Bucs' QB was too amped up and made too many mistakes. As long as Mayfield makes the proper pre-snap determinations, Tampa should have enough offensively to pull out a victory, even with Kyler Murray back in the Vikings' lineup.

Vikings: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Las Vegas Raiders (2-0) at New Orleans Saints (1-1)

The Las Vegas Raiders are sitting at 2-0, and while fans can argue that Las Vegas hasn't beaten a good team, so what? Learning how to beat the teams you're expected to beat is the first step in a rebuilding team's path to becoming a contender.

I just don't think that the New Orleans Saints are a team that the Raiders are supposed to beat. New Orleans is dangerous, and it should have a big crowd advantage in its home opener. I think we'll see a big discrepancy in quarterback play in this one, too.

Kirk Cousins is doing a nice job of being the Raiders' steady hand. Tyler Shough seems to be in the early stages of a Drake Maye-like Year 2 leap.

The Raiders are a surprise 2-0 team that's played well without All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who's expected to be back on the field Sunday, per Ian Rapoport .

Without Bowers, the Raiders have scored 26 and 27 points in their double-digit wins over the Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Chargers. With him, their offense should be more potent.

On the flip side, the Saints could feed off the energy of the crowd in their season home opener, and they're averaging a league-high 21 points in the second half of games. However, the Saints lost left tackle Kelvin Banks, which creates a favorable matchup for the Raiders' pass rush.

If you anticipate a close game, like this analyst, take the points with Las Vegas.

Saints: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell

Baltimore Ravens (1-1) at Dallas Cowboys (1-1) in Rio De Janeiro

Keep in mind that these teams will play in Rio De Janeiro at Maracanã Stadium. This matters because, going back to last season , the Dallas Cowboys offense is more than a field goal better at home than it is away from AT&T Stadium.

Furthermore, the Cowboys defense is still a leaky unit that's allowed close to 400 total yards in the team's first two games, ranking 29th in yards allowed.

Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters that players dealing with injuries have a "good shot" of playing in Brazil, including wideout Zay Flowers and left tackle Ronnie Stanley. If both are trending in the right direction, Dallas will have a hard time slowing down Lamar Jackson and the Ravens' passing attack.

I see this game coming down to the wire. The Ravens could absolutely open things up early and torch the Dallas defense if Zay Flowers is healthy enough to play near full fitness, but there's no guarantee he suits up (at the time of writing).

The Cowboys are struggling to run the ball, but Dak Prescott and the passing game can keep pace, and they haven't even gotten George Pickens going yet. This is a risky play, but the Ravens haven't shown me enough to trust them yet, and Big D is no stranger to shootouts.

Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

Los Angeles Rams (1-1) at Denver Broncos (1-1)

This game is going to be a rockfight—both teams have outstanding defenses, offenses that found a rhythm last week and a Denver Broncos team that was the AFC's No. 1 seed last year can't be happy about being a home underdog. The status of Puka Nacua looms large here as well. Wait, why did I take the Los Angeles Rams? The same reason most of my colleagues did—they're a better team.

The New York Giants were much more forgiving to a banged-up Rams receiver corps than Denver will be, especially considering Los Angeles is now on the road. The Broncos are due for a breakout performance, and I think it comes here.

Rams: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Philadelphia Eagles (2-0) at Chicago Bears (1-1)

This was supposed to be Caleb Williams against the Philadelphia Eagles in a potential NFC Championship preview. Now, with Williams out and Tyson Bagent dealing with a concussion, it looks like Case Keenum against Jalen Hurts. Much less exciting.

With Williams playing, I'd have given the Chicago Bears a shot here. But I can't see Keenum or Bagent scoring enough points to make up for a porous Bears defense. I think the Eagles offense has a big game on the road, and the Eagles win by at least a touchdown.

The Bears may roll with their third-string quarterback for this Monday Night Football matchup. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol.

While it seems like Philadelphia is the easy play because of Chicago's quarterback situation, don't forget that Eagles running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger last week and played limited snaps. As of Wednesday, his status for this matchup remains unclear.

Expect the Bears to rely heavily on their ground game led by D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai against the Eagles' run defense, which has allowed 101 and 115 yards to the Washington Commanders' and Tennessee Titans' running backs, respectively. Chicago dominates time of possession and keeps this game within a field goal.

Eagles: Davenport, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 3 Trade Value for This Year's Top 50 NFL Players
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football season has already been upended by an unfortunate amount of injuries, perhaps leaving your team in tatters—or perhaps giving you the opportunity to strike a favorable deal with an opposing player who suddenly has a huge need you can fill.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football season has already been upended by an unfortunate amount of injuries, perhaps leaving your team in tatters—or perhaps giving you the opportunity to strike a favorable deal with an opposing player who suddenly has a huge need you can fill.

Either way, the trade value chart exists to help ensure you don't get ripped off in prospective deals. It may feel early to be wheeling and dealing, but if the injury gods have already been unkind, well, you might not have much of a choice.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

We cannot ignore that injuries to players like Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart and Caleb Williams will have a ripple effect throughout fantasy football.

You have to immediately downgrade the skill players on the Giants, for instance. Going from Dart to Jameis Winston is a major downgrade, and the Los Angeles Rams were not scared to pack the box and shot down the run game. Cam Skattebo naturally gets a downgrade out of the top 50, while Malik Nabers stays on the chart—Winston has never been afraid to let it rip downfield—but loses some value.

Isaiah Likely didn't quite make the top-50 cut but he's still very much a TE1 going forward. The tight end position tends to weather backup quarterback situations a bit better than other positions and Likely leads the team in literally every receiving category, including targets (18).

Most of Washington's skill players weren't cracking the top 50 anyway, though Stefon Diggs was showing fantastic chemistry with Daniels. He remains more of a flex consideration with Daniels set for what seems likely to be a lengthy stint on the bench.

There's a bit more uncertainty with just how long Williams will be out, so you should be in a bit of a holding pattern when considering trades involving any of Chicago's fantasy options.

As for this week's climbers, keep in mind that we are very early into the season. But boy, does Josh Allen look like a potential fantasy MVP—and NFL MVP, for that matter—after two weeks. Averaging 38.2 points per game is wild work, and while torching Detroit's defense in Week 2 was hardly a surprise, he also put up obscene numbers against an elite Houston unit.

If Allen can sustain anything close to this level of production, he's going to quickly become one of the most valuable players in fantasy, if not most valuabe.

Kenneth Walker has also catapulted himself into the conversation for being one of the five most valuable players in all of fantasy. He currently leads the NFL in carries (47) and rushing yards (290), but it's also promising that Andy Reid and the Chiefs are involving him through the air (nine receptions for 79 yards and a score).

The Chiefs seem likely to keep pounding the rock with Walker, which has opened up the passing game in the process. Players like Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson still have higher ceilings considering how involved they'll remain in the passing game, but Walker's usage is extremely promising.

articles.title: 5 Trade Landing Spots for Marvin Harrison Jr. to Revive NFL Career
articles.summary: Within two years, Marvin Harrison Jr. has gone from a coveted college prospect, No. 4 overall pick in his draft class, to an afterthought in the Arizona Cardinals offense.
articles.body:
Within two years, Marvin Harrison Jr. has gone from a coveted college prospect, No. 4 overall pick in his draft class, to an afterthought in the Arizona Cardinals offense.

In two games this season, Harrison has seen just four targets, which is baffling given that general manager Monti Ossenfort used a premium draft pick on him to transform Arizona's passing offense.

Apparently, head coach Mike LaFleur, whom the team hired in February, has a different vision for the aerial attack, one in which Harrison isn't featured.

When asked about getting Harrison easier completions, LaFleur talked about the involvement of first-team All-Pro Trey McBride and wideout Kendrick Bourne on underneath routes.

Based on LaFleur's comments, Harrison isn't a priority in Arizona anymore. The Cardinals have already signed wideout Michael Wilson to a three-year, $75 million extension.

Next offseason, the Cardinals have to make a decision on whether to exercise the fifth-year option in Harrison's rookie deal, and it would be difficult to justify doing that if he sees a sharp decline in targets, which would also impact his production.

Harrison has drawn criticism for a lack of effort , which may be the first sign he wants out of Arizona. If that's the case, there are five destinations where the third-year pro can go to revive his NFL career.

The Baltimore Ravens would be a sleeper team among suitors. That said, general manager Eric DeCosta has a track record of being aggressive on the trade market.

On DeCosta's watch, the Ravens have acquired All-Pro cornerback Marcus Peters, linebacker Roquan Smith, who became a perennial All-Pro in Baltimore, and the team agreed to a trade for Las Vegas Raiders' five-time Pro Bowl pass-rusher Maxx Crosby, but backed out of it over concerns about his surgically repaired knee.

Assuming Harrison is healthy, DeCosta shouldn't have an issue with him as an addition to a receiver unit that featured Rashod Bateman as the No. 1 option last week.

Zay Flowers is battling a hamstring injury, and the team placed rookie third-round wideout Ja'Kobi Lane on injured reserve after he underwent surgery on a fractured wrist.

In the short term, Harrison can provide a much-needed boost to the Ravens' aerial attack. Even with a healthier unit, the 6'3", 220-pound receiver can be a more reliable target on the perimeter than Bateman while Flowers works out of the slot.

Because of Harrison's fading presence in the Cardinals offense, the Ravens could probably acquire him in exchange for a second-round pick, which is worth the gamble on a player with sky-high upside.

The Buffalo Bills have a crowded wide receiver unit with new acquisition DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Joshua Palmer and rookie fourth-rounder Skyler Bell. Still, with a Josh Allen-led offense, the Bills can make a work with the addition of another wideout.

In March, Bills general manager Brandon Beane traded a 2026 second-round pick to the Chicago Bears for Moore and a 2026 fifth-round pick. Keep in mind that Moore turned 29 in April and is coming off a down year, logging career lows in catches (50) and receiving yards (682) last season.

Beane may be willing to offer the best trade package for Harrison, a 24-year-old receiver who hasn't reached his peak. The Bills can exercise the fifth-year option on his rookie deal to keep him under team control for two more years while they figure out where he fits in their offense.

Unless Keon Coleman breaks out this year, Harrison can be the new featured target on the perimeter opposite Moore, with Shakir in the slot. It would be a well-rounded group of receivers with Harrison as the potential long-term centerpiece.

The Houston Texans are in a situation similar to the Baltimore Ravens. Although their long-term outlook at wide receiver looks promising, multiple players at the position are dealing with injuries.

Nico Collins has missed a game because of a hamstring issue. Jayden Higgins is out for the season with a torn ACL. Tank Dell is still recovering from multiple surgeries on knee injuries he suffered at the end of the 2024 season.

The Texans can reunite quarterback C.J. Stroud with Harrison to fill a glaring void in their offense. Leaving Arizona as the No. 3 option in the passing game, the Cardinals wideout could become Houston's go-to target until Collins returns.

With Stroud as his quarterback at Ohio State, Harrison set school records and was an all-timer on the college level. They can reconnect as a dynamic duo in the pros and elevate the Texans' mediocre passing attack.

As a sixth-year pro, Collins has yet to play all 17 games in a single season. Dell hasn't played a snap in nearly two years. Higgins will need to knock off some rust after sitting out a year. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will be free agents in 2027. Harrison could have a prominent role in the Texans' passing offense this year and beyond.

The Kansas City Chiefs have a new offensive identity with running back Kenneth Walker as the featured playmaker, but Patrick Mahomes is still one of the league's top quarterbacks.

If Mahomes gets a reliable receiver, he could once again lead the league in multiple passing categories, as he did years ago with Tyreek Hill as his top option. Harrison isn't in the same receiver mold as Hill, who can terrify defenders with blazing speed, though he can be a viable No. 1 target.

Don't forget that Harrison hauled in 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns in his 2024 rookie campaign. He hasn't lost his playmaking ability. If featured, the third-year pro can build on the promise many saw from him in his first season.

In Kansas City, Harrison would play under renowned play-calling head coach Andy Reid, and he could immediately command a high target share.

In part because of injuries and a suspension, Rashee Rice has been inconsistent. Though even while healthy for the first two games of this campaign, he's seen eight targets, two in Week 1. Xavier Worthy has seen a healthy share of targets (13), but he's been unable to convert those opportunities into high production, with eight catches for just 43 yards and a touchdown.

Rice is in a contract year, and he hasn't done enough to earn a big-money extension. Kelce looks rejuvenated, but he turns 37 in October. Harrison can be a foundational piece of the Chiefs' aerial attack beyond the current season, while regaining his mojo as a valuable asset in Reid's offense.

Based on position need, the Las Vegas Raiders make the most sense for Harrison in the short and long term. Unlike the other teams, the Raiders don't have a major investment in any of their wide receivers. The club signed Jalen Nailor to a three-year, $35 million deal this past offseason, and he's the highest earner within the unit.

Tre Tucker will be a free agent in 2027. Jack Bech, a second-rounder from the 2025 draft, has made plays, but he hasn't shown signs of being a high-volume pass-catcher.

For now, All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers is clearly the Raiders' best pass-catcher, though he's missed time because of knee injuries over the last year. The Raiders can take some of the offensive workload off him with the addition of a potential No. 1 wideout.

With a 2-0 start, Las Vegas may be better than many expected under first-time head coach Klint Kubiak, who's leading a young team in the early stages of another franchise rebuild. Harrison's career timeline fits with the start of the Raiders' roster reset.

Still budding with promise, Harrison can grow with a young Raiders' squad on the upswing. General manager John Spytek can give the wideout a trial run as the lead receiver for a below-average unit and decide what to do with the option year in his contract next offseason.

If Harrison makes significant strides, the Silver and Black would have a long-term one-two combination at receiver and tight end for rookie Fernando Mendoza when he's ready to take over the offense. Assuming Las Vegas uses nothing more than a Day 2 pick on Harrison, it can still take a receiver in the first round of the draft or address another priority roster need.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Week 3 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em, Play or Bench Advice on Top Fantasy Football NFL Stars
articles.summary: Week 3 will get underway on Thursday night with a battle between the Atlanta Falcons and Green Bay Packers. It's an intriguing matchup because it'll mark the return of Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr.. His return could have serious fantasy implications.
articles.body:
Week 3 will get underway on Thursday night with a battle between the Atlanta Falcons and Green Bay Packers. It's an intriguing matchup because it'll mark the return of Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr.. His return could have serious fantasy implications.

Poor quarterback play has hampered fantasy stars Bijan Robinson, Kyle Pitts, and Drake London. Ideally, Penix will help return them to form, though Robinson remains the only true must-start of the bunch for now.

Who else can managers rely on in Week 3? Let's dive into the recent production and the matchups for some start/sit recommendations. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens will play in Brazil on Sunday afternoon, and the travel and change of venue could throw the two teams off. However, managers should still expect a strong outing from Dak Prescott and the Cowboys offense. Otherwise, Dallas isn't going to stay in this game.

The Ravens have enough offensive firepower to make this a high-scoring game, and their defense has surrendered an average of 16.2 fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.

Even with Puka Nacua out of the lineup, Matthew Stafford managed to have a bounce-back game against the New York Giants on Monday night. However, he'll face a much stiffer challenge in Denver against the Broncos.

Expect Denver to do a much better job of limiting Davante Adams, which could leave Stafford with rather pedestrian numbers. Other Week 3 QB sits:

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

The New York Giants will be without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the foreseeable future. This means that they'll need to lean heavily on the run to support backup Jameis Winston.

The Tennessee Titans have been fairly respectable against the run thus far, surrendering an average of 20 fantasy points to opposing backfields. However, a heavy workload will raise Skattebo's value significantly.

MarShawn Lloyd has largely disappointed as the Packers' starting running back. He did find the end zone in Week 2, but he also fumbled while averaging just 3.3 yards per carry. Kaleb Johnson looked like the stronger runner, and he could eat into Lloyd's workload significantly this week.

The Falcons, meanwhile, have surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs. Other RBs to sit in Week 3:

OK, so we said that the Broncos are likely to do a decent job of limiting Adams. That just means that he's probably not going to go off for eight catches, 195 yards, and two touchdowns this week.

Adams is still going to get peppered with targets, and he's going to remain a strong start for as long as Nacua is out. Other WR starts for Week 3:

Chicago Bears wideout Rome Odunze has been a low-end flex option to this point, but his value took a massive hit when Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury on Sunday. Backup QB Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol , too, meaning Case Keenum could see his first game action since 2003.

Unless Williams makes an unexpected return to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, Odunze will be unplayable.

Nico Collins is expected to miss the Houston Texans' Week 3 matchup with the rival Indianapolis Colts. That could mean another massive game for tight end Dalton Schultz.

Schultz served as C.J. Stroud's go-to target during last week's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. He finished with 12 catches and 140 yards. The Colts, meanwhile, have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

Sit: Harold Fannin Jr., Cleveland Browns

The Cleveland Browns have found some viable wide receivers in rookies Denzel Boston and K.C. Concepcion. However, that has hurt the value of Harold Fannin Jr., who has just seven catches and 75 yards through two weeks.

Fannin could still regain his 2025 form if Deshaun Watson can keep playing at an average level as he did in Week 2. This week, though, the Browns host the Carolina Panthers, who have surrendered the ninth-fewest fantasy points to opposing TEs.

articles.title: Week 3 Fantasy Football Cheat Sheet for Deep NFL Sleepers to Target
articles.summary: We're already at the doorstep of Week 3, and some fantasy managers may be scrambling to fill in starting lineups. The past week brought more injuries, and there is no shortage of uncertain statuses entering the weekend.
articles.body:
We're already at the doorstep of Week 3, and some fantasy managers may be scrambling to fill in starting lineups. The past week brought more injuries, and there is no shortage of uncertain statuses entering the weekend.

Fortunately, some deep sleepers may still be available on the waiver wire.

Here, you'll find updated rankings for Week 2, a cheat sheet of potential value starts, and a look at some top waiver targets. All rankings and picks are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Sleeper: Bryce Young, QB, Carolina Panthers

Managers who lost Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, or Jaxson Dart to injury in Week 2 may need to find a plug-and-play starter off the waiver wire. Carolina Panthers signal-caller Bryce Young could be the perfect option.

Young has been fantastic to this point, passing for 648 yards and a league-high six touchdowns (tied). He has also added a rushing score.

This week, Young will face a Cleveland Browns defense that looked competent in Week 2 but was a total disaster in Week 1. He'll be on the road in an unfriendly environment, but it's hard to envision Young totally flopping this week.

The Browns have surrendered an average of 19.5 fantasy points to opposing QBs. Young is rostered in only 41 percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Adonai Mitchell, WR, New York Jets

New York Jets wide receiver Adonai Mitchell has topped 60 receiving yards in each of the first two weeks, and he's coming off a six-reception game against the Green Bay Packers. Those aren't eye-popping numbers, but Mitchell has legitimate flex value in Week 3.

The Jets are set to visit the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing wide receivers. The Lions are also likely to focus heavily on limiting No. 1 Jets receiver Garrett Wilson, which should give Mitchell some big-play opportunities.

The third-year receiver is still a bit of a risk-reward option because New York could lean on the run in an effort to keep Detroit's offense off the field. However, he's worth a flier in a week that could be without several top quarterbacks and wide receivers like Puka Nacua and Nico Collins.

Michell is rostered in just 19 percent of leagues.
