articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 3 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: Following a week with several injuries, many fantasy managers are in need of sleepers to fill spots for Week 3. Fortunately, it's still early in the season, and there are plenty of options widely available in the free-agent pool.
articles.body:
Following a week with several injuries, many fantasy managers are in need of sleepers to fill spots for Week 3. Fortunately, it's still early in the season, and there are plenty of options widely available in the free-agent pool.

By this time next week, it may be too late to add a rookie wide receiver who has caught a touchdown reception in both of his games. Don't be late to the party, even if the host has an underwhelming offense.

Because of favorable matchups, two other rookies could see expanded roles, one of them in a game that's projected to be the third-highest scoring contest on Sunday's slate.

Lastly, a once-prominent running back for point-per-reception leagues resurfaces as a flex option. On the other side of 30, he's still fantasy-relevant in a backup role.

Here are the biggest sleepers at every position—all of them available in more than 50 percent of PPR leagues, according to FantasyPros .

QB Geno Smith at Detroit Lions (6 Percent Rostered)

If the New York Jets have any chance to keep pace with the Detroit Lions' fourth-ranked scoring offense, Geno Smith must push the ball downfield. Last week, Gang Green struggled to establish its run game against the Green Bay Packers, averaging just 2.5 yards per carry.

This week, offensive coordinator Frank Reich should have a simple plan to attack the glaring weakness in the Lions' injury-riddled secondary. Detroit is still without its starting safeties, All-Pro Kerby Joseph and Pro Bowler Brian Branch.

Before Smith's disastrous 2025 season with the Las Vegas Raiders, he had a strong track record playing indoors.

According to The Athletic's Mike Sando , the veteran signal-caller threw for 30 touchdowns and five interceptions with a 110.8 passer rating in 14 road starts with the Seattle Seahawks.

Behind the Jets' high-end pass-protecting offensive line , Smith could have a productive outing in a high-scoring matchup.

RB Alvin Kamara vs. Las Vegas Raiders (39 Percent Rostered)

It's a new day and age when Alvin Kamara is considered a sleeper option. Once upon a time, he was one of the best fantasy assets in PPR leagues. Now, the 31-year-old running back is a backup for Travis Etienne, whom the New Orleans Saints signed to a four-year, $48 million deal this past offseason.

Coming off a sprained MCL, Kamara made his season debut last week against the Baltimore Ravens, recording nine carries for 15 yards and five catches for seven yards.

Yes, Kamara posted an inefficient fantasy stat line, but he had 14 touches in his first game back from injury, which is likely an indication that the 10-year pro will have a solid role as the Saints' No. 2 tailback and lead pass-catcher out of the backfield.

Expect Kamara to have more juice in the Saints' season home opener on Sunday. As one of the most productive running backs in the passing game, he has a high floor as a fantasy flex option. It's also worth noting that Etienne is dealing with a hamstring injury and could yield more touches to his established backup.

RB Emmett Johnson at Miami Dolphins (24 Percent Rostered)

Running back Kenneth Walker has garnered most of the attention in the Kansas City Chiefs' new-look backfield, but his backup has looked impressive as well.

Rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson showed off his smooth moves on the ground in the Chiefs' Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Head coach Andy Reid could reward Johnson with more touches going forward (h/t A to Z Sports' Charles Goldman ).

Based on FanDuel's odds , the Chiefs are 10.5-point favorites over the Miami Dolphins. They look dominant again and could build a multiscore lead pretty quickly in this matchup. If so, don't be surprised if Reid gives Walker a breather and unleashes Johnson on the ground to work the clock.

WR Denzel Boston vs. Carolina Panthers (48 Percent Rostered)

You may already be late to hop on the Denzel Boston hype train, but he's still widely available and should be rostered in a lot more leagues. The rookie first-rounder is emerging as the Cleveland Browns' lead outside receiver.

Boston is tied with KC Concepcion for a team-leading 11 targets and has three fewer receptions than his draftmate, but he leads the Browns with 154 receiving yards and has scored in both games.

For those wary of picking up a Browns player, Cleveland's offense showed signs of life in a 23-19 road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. In Week 3, the Browns will play their home opener against the Carolina Panthers, who gave up 59 points to the Chicago Bears just two weeks ago. The Browns offense doesn't compare to the Bears' unit, but Boston could be busy in a surprisingly high-scoring contest.

Panthers quarterback Bryce Young is one of four signal-callers with a league-leading six touchdown passes. If he stays hot, the Browns may have to match his production with their passing game, which would bode well for Boston's fantasy ceiling in Week 3.

WR Xavier Hutchinson at Indianapolis Colts (8 Percent Rostered)

After the Houston Texans ruled out wide receiver Nico Collins, most fantasy managers picked up Kayshon Boutte, given the fact that the team acquired him from the New England Patriots on the heels of Jayden Higgins' season-ending knee injury.

Although Boutte saw an increased snap count of about 27 percent between Weeks 1 and 2, Xavier Hutchinson saw the second-most targets behind tight end Dalton Schultz last week.

While it's logical to hold on to Boutte, remember that Hutchinson has a stronger rapport with quarterback C.J. Stroud. Boutte has only been with the team for a month. Stroud and Hutchinson are in their fourth season together.

If the Texans' Week 2 target share is any indication of which receiver has the best chance at a breakout performance in Collins' absence, Hutchinson should be on your sleeper radar.

WR Darius Slayton vs. Houston Texans (1 Percent Rostered)

Fantasy managers brave enough to take a deep dive into the sleeper pool should consider Darius Slayton.

The Indianapolis Colts signed Slayton on Monday after the team found out that wide receiver Alec Pierce aggravated a heel injury early in last Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Slayton isn't an ordinary free-agent fill-in for the Colts. He has a rapport with quarterback Daniel Jones. Both drafted by the New York Giants in 2019, they played together for six seasons.

With Jones as his quarterback for most of the 2019, 2020 and 2022 campaigns, Slayton racked up 724-plus receiving yards and led Big Blue with eight touchdown receptions in his rookie year.

Averaging 15 yards per reception, Slayton can mimic some of what Pierce has done as a big-play receiver. He'll face the Houston Texans' uncharacteristically porous pass defense that's allowed the most fantasy points to wide receivers in two weeks.

TE Kenyon Sadiq at Detroit Lions (34 Percent Rostered)

Last week, New York Jets wide receiver Adonai Mitchell made the sleeper list, and he has another favorable matchup this week, but for the sake of variance, take a look at Kenyon Sadiq.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , tight end Mason Taylor is dealing with a thumb injury. As a result, Sadiq could play a bigger role against the Detroit Lions.

Despite Sadiq's limited time on the field, he scored on a three-yard run in the Jets' season opener. If the coaching staff continues to manufacture touches for him, he could be primed for a big day against the Lions' pass defense, which has allowed the second-most yards and fourth-most touchdowns.

For context, the Lions allowed the New Orleans Saints' and Buffalo Bills' top two tight ends to score a touchdown apiece in their two games. In a crush spot, Sadiq could produce TE1 numbers.

TE Oronde Gadsden at Buffalo Bills (17 Percent Rostered)

The Los Angeles Chargers placed David Njoku on injured reserve, and Charlie Kolar fractured his left forearm, which leaves Oronde Gadsden as the top tight end on the depth chart.

As a rookie in the previous season, Gadsden caught 49 passes for 664 yards and three touchdowns. Now in a much less crowded tight end room compared to just a week ago, he should be in line for a decent target share, especially with wideout Ladd McConkey fully practicing and playing through a rib injury.

The Chargers will need healthy pass-catchers to match touchdown drives with the Buffalo Bills' league-leading scoring offense. That said, Buffalo is also prone to giving up points and yards, specifically to tight ends.

In Week 2, the Bills allowed six catches for 52 yards and a touchdown to Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta. Gadsden can put up those numbers and more if he's a featured pass-catcher in the banged-up Chargers offense.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: There are plenty of reasons for fans to worry as the NFL hits Week 3. Here are 5 things to watch
articles.summary: It’s the third week of the NFL season and some issues are becoming blatantly apparent as teams start to figure out their identities.
articles.body: It’s the third week of the NFL season and some issues are becoming blatantly apparent as teams start to figure out their identities. In some places, injuries are piling up and threatening to derail teams before the season gets out of its first month. In others, there are clear personnel issues that are flashing warning signs about what the future may hold. And in Atlanta, everyone’s just mad. Here are five things to watch in Week 3 of the NFL season. How will the Giants, Commanders and Bears cope with backup QBs? It was a tough Week 2 for the New York Giants, Washington Commanders and Chicago Bears as each team saw their starting quarterback knocked out of their games with injuries. It seems like it’s only going to be worse this week. The Bears host the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night and might be playing with their third-string quarterback. Caleb Williams left Sunday’s loss to the Minnesota Vikings with a hamstring injury (he’s week-to-week) and backup Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol and also could miss Sunday’s game. That leaves Case Keenum as the next man up to face a ferocious Philly defense in a primetime game. It’s a brutal early season situation for a team that was widely seen as favorites in the NFC North this year. The Commanders and Giants will also face difficult situations as Jayden Daniels (dislocated left elbow) and Jaxson Dart (knee injury) are both out. Daniels dislocated the same elbow that he injured in 2025, causing him to miss about half the season, just before halftime of Sunday’s loss against Dallas. He’ll miss Week 3 against Seattle with Marcus Mariota taking over starting duties against the defending Super Bowl champions. It’s unclear when Daniels might return as he is seeing specialists about his elbow and the Commanders aren’t working on a specific timeframe. Dart and the Giants face a similar situation. While initial signs were good after Dart took a big hit to his left knee on the opening drive of Monday’s game against the Rams – he walked off under his own power and returned to the sidelines in street clothes – Tuesday brought devastating news for his team. Dart’s injury is feared to be worse than initially thought and he could end up missing significant time, if not the whole season. The Giants were hoping for a big turnaround under head coach John Harbaugh and Dart was a big part of those plans. They take on the lowly Tennessee Titans on Sunday in New Jersey, giving Jameis Winston a chance to get his feet under him as the new starter in the Meadowlands. The Lions’ defense is a mess taking on a familiar face Detroit Lions fans at Ford Field on Sunday might look across at the opposing sideline and long for the face they see there: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn. Glenn was Detroit’s defensive coordinator under head coach Dan Campbell from 2021 to 2024 and a key part of a coaching staff that led a massive turnaround in fortunes in the Motor City as the Lions became Super Bowl contenders. The defense under Glenn was never lockdown, but it was serviceable. Since he left to take the Jets’ head coaching job, Detroit’s defense has been shambolic. The Lions allowed more than 24 points per game in 2025, 22nd in the league. Big plays abounded, the team struggled to get off the field on third down and injuries hurt the unit. It all led to a 9-8 record and the Lions missing the playoffs. So far, things aren’t much better this year. Through two games, the Lions have the second-worst defense in the league – though facing Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on a short week seven days ago didn’t help their stats. The Lions are struggling to stop the pass, struggling to stop the run, are allowing lengthy drives and are – once again – facing injuries to key players. The Jets aren’t exactly setting the world on fire offensively, but quarterback Geno Smith has feasted on the Lions defense in the past during his time in Seattle. Sunday’s game could be a sign of where Detroit is headed this year; the team’s offense looks supercharged once again behind Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown, but they’ll only go as far as the defense allows them to go. Misery in Atlanta is about to play out on national TV Things in Atlanta are … not great. The Falcons’ quarterback situation is abysmal. Michael Penix Jr. missed the first two games of the season while recovering from last year’s torn ACL. Tua Tagovailoa was slated to start the season and then started having oblique spasms days before the opener and also missed those two games. Cooper Rush filled in and proceeded to throw four interceptions and never going over 150 yards in losses to the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers. Jack Strand came in against Carolina and he was bad too, throwing another pick. The team is 0-2, getting blown out in its home opener to boos from the Atlanta faithful. Vibes are bad, and the future doesn’t exactly look promising. So, of course, the Falcons are going to be on national TV for their next three games. Thursday night’s game against the Packers starts the stretch as the Dirty Birds head to Lambeau Field with Penix expected to make his first start of the season. Then after a week off, the Falcons will head to New Orleans to face their NFC South rivals on October 5 before hosting the Baltimore Ravens in the Sunday night game on October 11. Falcons fans have been dreading the start of the season ever since the decision to pick up Tagovailoa in the offseason, which immediately created a quarterback controversy with Penix as two often-injured players would compete for the starting job. Those low expectations have been justified by the poor start to the season and it seems like the misery is about to go national. The NFL’s weekly international sojourn begins A record-breaking nine NFL games will be played out of the US in 2026, and the international schedule really gets going in earnest this week. The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers got their seasons started in Australia, but when the Ravens and Cowboys kick off in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday, it will mark the start of eight straight weeks of international action. Sunday’s showdown at the famous Maracanā Stadium in Rio is the first time the NFL has played a game at one of the most legendary venues in all of global sport. The Maracanā has hosted two World Cup finals, saw Brazil men’s soccer win an Olympic gold medal during the 2016 Rio Games, where it hosted the opening and closing ceremonies, held countless major concerts and soccer matches, and is generally one of the most celebrated venues in the world. It’s nice that the NFL sent two teams that could put on an exciting game for the Brazilian fans, one that could match the prestige of the venue. The Ravens and Cowboys are expected to compete for the top spots in their divisions, and the quarterback matchup of Lamar Jackson vs. Dak Prescott is pure box office. Prescott has started this season hot and leads the league in passing touchdowns, and Jackson is off to a similarly blistering start after torching the Saints and Indianapolis Colts in the first two games. Following this week’s game in Brazil, the NFL heads to Europe for three games in London then individual games in Paris, Madrid and Munich. The international slate wraps up with that game in Germany on November 15 when the Cincinnati Bengals and Lions face off. Someone’s 0 has got to go (probably) The AFC South is not good this year. The Jacksonville Jaguars are 1-1 and are the only team in the division with a win. The Titans, Houston Texans and Colts are all 0-2. That most likely will change on Sunday. The Texans and Colts will face off in Indy in a game that, theoretically, one team has to win (a tie is possible and would make life worse for both teams). The stakes are particularly high for the Texans, a team that was expected to compete for a playoff spot this year but have so far been unable to stop two of the top teams in the AFC in losses to the Bills and Bengals. The Colts suffered a heartbreaker in Kansas City in Week 2, losing in overtime to the Chiefs. Indianapolis hopes to take another major step after finishing 8-9 last year, including challenging the Texans for the top spot in the division and returning to the playoffs for the first time since the 2020-2021 season. The odds for a playoff berth will be stacked against whoever loses this game on Sunday – only seven teams in NFL history have made the playoffs after starting 0-3. And two of those teams happens to be the 2018 and 2025 Houston Texans, so there’s still always hope deep in the heart of Texas. Full Week 3 schedule Thursday Atlanta Falcons @ Green Bay Packers, 8:15 p.m. ET Sunday Cincinnati Bengals @ Pittsburgh Steelers, 1 p.m. ET New England Patriots @ Jacksonville Jaguars, 1 p.m. ET Tennessee Titans @ New York Giants, 1 p.m. ET Seattle Seahawks @ Washington Commanders, 1 p.m. ET New York Jets @ Detroit Lions, 1 p.m. ET Carolina Panthers @ Cleveland Browns, 1 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs @ Miami Dolphins, 1 p.m. ET Los Angeles Chargers @ Buffalo Bills, 1 p.m. ET Houston Texans @ Indianapolis Colts, 1 p.m. ET Arizona Cardinals @ San Francisco 49ers, 4:05 p.m. ET Minnesota Vikings @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 4:05 p.m. ET Las Vegas Raiders @ New Orleans Saint, 4:25 p.m. ET Baltimore Ravens @ Dallas Cowboys, 4:25 p.m. ET Los Angeles Rams @ Denver Broncos, 8:20 p.m. ET Monday Philadelphia Eagles @ Chicago Bears, 8:15 p.m. ET

articles.title: From a $200,000 goal to $41.6 million raised, J.J. Watt’s Hurricane Harvey effort became a defining chapter of his NFL legacy
articles.summary: When Hurricane Harvey tore through Houston in August 2017, J.J. Watt did not wait for someone else to act.
articles.body: When Hurricane Harvey tore through Houston in August 2017, J.J. Watt did not wait for someone else to act. The defensive end posted a fundraising goal of $200,000 on social media. Within days, donations started pouring in from across the country. What began as a modest target quickly became one of the most remarkable athlete-led relief efforts in American sports history, eventually crossing $41.6 million and reaching hundreds of thousands of people whose lives the storm had upended.How did J.J. Watt raise $41.6 million for Hurricane Harvey relief?The number still sounds almost impossible when you say it out loud. Two hundred thousand dollars was the original ask. J.J. Watt hit that figure so fast he kept raising the ceiling, first to $1 million, then higher, until the campaign took on a life of its own. Donations came from all 50 states and more than 25 countries. NFL players contributed. Fans who had never watched a football game in their lives sent in $5 and $10 because something about Watt's straightforward appeal cut through the noise.Watt himself was direct about where the money would go. No vague promises. The funds were distributed to four non-profit organizations: Feeding America, Save the Children, Direct Relief, and Americares. Each group had existing infrastructure in the region, which meant aid moved faster than it would have through a newly created body. That decision mattered enormously in the early weeks when families were still living in shelters and waiting for basic supplies.By the time the campaign closed, more than 200,000 individuals and families had received some form of assistance. Meals were delivered. Medical care reached people who had no other option. Children caught in the chaos of displacement got support that might have taken months to arrive otherwise. Watt never framed it as charity. He talked about it the way Houstonians talk about each other during a crisis: you help because that is just what you do.What was the long-term impact of J.J. Watt's Hurricane Harvey Fund on Houston?The money itself told only part of the story. What Watt built in those frantic weeks after Harvey was a template for how athletes could use their platform in a genuine, accountable way. He posted regular updates. He pushed back against those who questioned where the money was going. He kept the process transparent long after the news cycle had moved on.Houston remembered. When Watt eventually left the Texans in 2021, the city's response reflected something deeper than athletic appreciation. He had shown up for the community in a way that went far beyond the football field, and people did not forget that.The $41.6 million figure is the one most people remember. But the real measure of what the fund accomplished lives in the quieter details. A family that got back into their home six months earlier than expected. A child who had access to school meals during a period when everything else had fallen apart. articles.title: Caleb Williams' repost dismissed antisemitic incident involving Dave Portnoy – and almost no one cares
articles.summary: Caleb Williams reposted a comment on X that dismissed an antisemitic incident involving Dave Portnoy, raising questions about double standards in sports.
articles.body: Most people — including Bears quarterback Caleb Williams — probably didn't think much of it. To them, it's just a repost on X that went after a common target for keyboard warriors. But what if it's more than that? Earlier in the week, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy mocked Williams, calling him a "thespian" after he was carted off the field for what was revealed to be a hamstring strain. Portnoy said the emotion Williams displayed was akin to what you'd see for a season-ending injury such as an ACL tear, not a tweak that's put him on a week-to-week basis. CALEB WILLIAMS AVOIDS MAJOR HAMSTRING INJURY AS MRI REVEALS A STRAIN BUT NO TEAR AFTER VIKINGS GAME SCARE Williams didn't take too kindly to the call-out, and went after Dave on X — using not his own words but those of a poster named Daemar. ''The guy that had a kid arrested and expelled from school for throwing pennies at him is calling someone else soft LMFAOOOOOO," Daemar said of Portnoy. Williams reposted the comment — which garnered 1.3 million views and 35K likes — to little media or fan criticism. Except ... Daemar was running cover for a clear antisemite. Here's a more thorough explanation. In the fall of 2025, Mississippi State student Patrick McClintock was caught on camera yelling "F—k the Jews!" before tossing coins at Portnoy, who's Jewish. This wasn't a random gesture. The American Jewish Committee made note that such coin-tossing is an "age-old antisemitic trope about Jews and greed." Portnoy posted a video of the affair and condemned the act — calling the student a "loser" while decrying an uptick in his personal antisemitic experiences. As Outkick's Armando Salguero pointed out, McClintock was later arrested independently for disturbing the peace. In other words, Portnoy blasted an antisemite in a time when antisemitism is on the clear rise. Sorry, but that does not disqualify you from ridiculing a quarterback for being melodramatic. REPORTER FOR THE ATHLETIC FUMES OVER ARCH MANNING, SILENT ON JOSH JACOBS' ALLEGED VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMAN Portnoy has since responded to Williams' repost by accusing him of spreading misinformation about him. And though he seemed to make a peace offering by saying "I will not hold this against Caleb...I'm rooting for him and all of Chicago," one has to wonder what the response would have been like if the repost had been in a different context. For instance, if there had been a highly publicized anti-Black incident on a college campus, I doubt reposting an X user dismissing the affair would be treated so warmly by social media users. If there had been a homophobic or anti-woman gesture, there likely would have been a media uproar if a prominent athlete condoned it. Look what happened to Texas quarterback Arch Manning when he laughed at an AI meme involving ESPN's Holly Rowe getting slapped by Steve Sarkisian. He was shamed into apologizing for something that was fake. Portnoy being blatantly discriminated against for being Jewish was very real. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Emails attempting to reach the Bears and NFL for comment were not returned, and that's understandable. Williams probably didn't know exactly what he was reposting, and giving this matter any extra attention doesn't help the team or the league. It's also predictable that much of the public seems to side with Williams on this issue. They probably don't know the full extent of what Portnoy — a highly polarizing figure — endured in Starkville that day. But it is noteworthy how different types of discrimination are treated. Some are condemned swiftly and harshly, others are shrugged off almost entirely. Portnoy has been a strong critic of cancel culture and clearly doesn't want to see Williams suffer anymore than he has. He took the path of forgiveness and will be better off for it. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Unfortunately, there are a lot of people who don't think Williams needs forgiveness. They simply don't think he did anything wrong.

articles.title: Jameis Winston ready to embrace ‘beautiful’ opportunity to fill in for Jaxson Dart as Giants QB
articles.summary: Jameis Winston isn’t happy to see Jaxson Dart go out for the rest of the season, but is relishing the opportunity to play as the New York Giants’ starting qu...
articles.body:
Jameis Winston isn't happy to see Jaxson Dart go out for the rest of the season, but is relishing the opportunity to play as the New York Giants ' starting quarterback.

Dart has suffered multiple knee injuries that require knee surgery, thus ruling him out for the rest of the season.

This means that the Giants will have to rely on Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback for the remainder of the season.

Jameis Winston ready to step up and deliver for the New York Giants

Speaking to reporters ahead of the New York Giants' game against the Arizona Cardinals this weekend, Jameis Winston reflected on becoming the new starting quarterback.

Despite his sadness and empathy for Jaxson Dart, Winston admitted that this was the opportunity and moment that he was dreaming of.

"This is what I have always dreamed of: to be a starting quarterback. Obviously, my respect and gratitude is going to be with Jaxson.

"But at the same time, this is what I dreamed of. I dream of being where I am right now and executing at a high level.

"The opportunity is beautiful. It's amazing. I'm grateful for it. But at the same time, I've got a brother that I've got to keep lifted up, and I have to prepare for a football game."

While Winston would have hoped that this opportunity came under more positive circumstances, he certainly cannot afford to squander this chance.

After the way his career has panned out following his exit from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , this could be the season he plays the most games since 2019.

After leaving the Buccaneers, Winston has only played double-digit regular-season games once, during the 2024 season with the Cleveland Browns .

For the most part, Winston's injuries and overall lack of consistent performances have relegated him to being the second-string quarterback across the 2020s.

With the Giants, Winston has a chance to remind teams in the NFL that he can be a reliable quarterback when given the chance.

But for that to happen, he needs to be able to deliver for them at the highest level possible, and ensuring that they win games during this run.

articles.title: "Screw these kids up": Tom Brady's controversial parenting stance ignites debate over kids, failure and success
articles.summary: Tom Brady knows what it takes to turn setbacks into success.
articles.body: Tom Brady knows what it takes to turn setbacks into success. The seven-time Super Bowl champion built an NFL career that few could have predicted when he entered the league as the 199th overall pick in 2000. Now, the former quarterback has a message for parents who want to see their children succeed. Brady believes shielding kids from failure could hold them back, and he is putting that belief into practice while raising his three children.Tom Brady criticised modern parenting and the fear of failureLast year, Tom Brady shared his views during a conversation with Fortune editor-in-chief Alyson Shontell at the Fortune Global Forum in New York. He questioned a parenting trend that, in his view, allows children to avoid challenges instead of learning how to overcome them.“Think of today’s world, how we screw these kids up,” Brady told Fortune editor-in-chief Alyson Shontell. “Every time they mess up, we send them to an easier place to succeed.”For Brady, the problem goes beyond sports. When children face competition or struggle to meet expectations, moving them to an easier environment may offer short-term relief. But it can also take away the chance to develop patience, resilience and confidence.His own journey offers a clear example. Brady spent his high school years working to earn the starting quarterback role, rather than expecting it to come easily. He believes those demanding experiences helped shape the player he became.“We’ve all faced different challenges in life; we’ve all faced our own adversities,” he said. “Look at the hardest things that have ever happened. We look back at those and realize they’re the best things that could’ve happened.”Brady also credited the challenges he faced before reaching the NFL for helping him build a career that spanned 23 seasons.Tom Brady explained why his children need challengesBrady's parenting philosophy is rooted in the support he received from his own parents. They encouraged him to pursue football, even when success seemed far from certain, without pushing him towards an easier alternative.“The blessing my parents gave: When I was that long-shot as a kid who was a backup quarterback, they never said, man, don’t do that, it’ll be too hard, think about another backup plan,” Brady said. “They said, go for it—that’s probably my parenting style.”That approach also reflects Brady's views on leadership. During his playing career, he wanted teammates to push beyond their limits, stay humble after victories and remain eager to learn from mistakes.For Brady, helping children succeed does not mean removing every obstacle. It means giving them the support to face difficulties, learn from disappointment and keep going. articles.title: ‘Not a Good Look,’ ‘It’s Disheartening’ — NFL Legend Terrell Owens Urges Shaquille O’Neal To Give Back Honorary FBI Badge, Calling It ‘Trash’
articles.summary: Shaquille O’Neal’s long association with law enforcement has come under scrutiny after accepting an honorary FBI Special Agent badge. The ceremonial recognit...
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal's long association with law enforcement has come under scrutiny after accepting an honorary FBI Special Agent badge. The ceremonial recognition quickly sparked backlash online, and former NFL star Terrell Owens believes O'Neal made things worse with his response to critics.

Terrell Owens Wants Shaq to Return FBI Badge

Speaking on the "Get To the Point Podcast," Owens criticized O'Neal after FBI Director Kash Patel presented the former NBA and Los Angeles Laker star with an honorary FBI Special Agent badge and plaque during the FBI National Academy's Session 299 graduation ceremony on September 17 in Quantico, Virginia.

Patel praised O'Neal during the ceremony as "one of the best supporters of law enforcement in the country." Owens, however, took issue with the timing of the recognition and O'Neal's response to the backlash.

"And for me, this is disheartening what Shaq did, especially in response to this guy," Owens said on the podcast , referring to Shaq's DM to a guy who burned his jersey as a form of protest.

Owens added that O'Neal could have accepted the honor at another time, saying, "There's timing to everything. There's a time and a place for everything. Maybe you could have gotten this award some other time, but this wasn't the time to do it."

The former NFL star also criticized O'Neal for his response to people who questioned the recognition, particularly his comments mocking their financial situations.

"You're demeaning. You're belittling somebody. You're demeaning people," Owens said. "If that's the case, he's talking to me. I ain't got no billion dollars. I'm broke, too. If that's the case, everybody's broke when compared to him."

Owens said he expected O'Neal to eventually address the controversy and offered him an opportunity to do so on the podcast. "I think, honestly, this is just not a good look," he said, adding that O'Neal could come on the show and explain himself.

Co-host Chris Spencer then made his position clear with a joke, pointing to a trash can where O'Neal could drop his badge after coming on the show. "And we have a little trash can for your badge," Spencer said.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Owens followed with an even blunter assessment. "That badge, right? That badge is trash," he said, again questioning whether the current political climate was the right moment to accept an honorary agent badge.

Reacting to a clip from the podcast on X, Owens also wrote , "Shaq, We ALL make mistakes or just have poor judgment at times, ME included. BUT…. It's not too late to give that badge back."

O'Neal's ties to law enforcement stretch back more than two decades, including reserve-officer roles in California and Florida and a sheriff's deputy appointment in Georgia.

articles.title: POLL: Should the Lions re-sign RB Jamaal Williams?
articles.summary: Jamaal Williams wants to return to the NFL and has interest in the Detroit Lions. Should they re-sign the veteran RB?
articles.body:
On Wednesday, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press dropped an article revealing that former Detroit Lions running back Jamaal Williams is attempting to a comeback in the NFL after being out of the league in 2025. Williams told Birkett that he called up Lions coach Dan Campbell about a possible reunion with the team , but Campbell said they were sticking with the running backs they currently have at the moment.

Those running backs are Jahmyr Gibbs , Sione Vaki , and Jacob Saylors —with Jabari Small on the practice squad. While true the Lions are down their initial backup running back in Isiah Pacheco , who is out until December with a back injury, Detroit has adjusted to that injury by increasing Gibbs' overall role and using Vaki as the next man up. It may not have the flash of Sonic and Knuckles, but Gibbs has been effective and Vaki is growing into his role.

But Williams was undeniably an important piece of the offense in 2021 and 2022. Besides being a vocal leader and an entertaining personality, he was also a short-yardage and touchdown machine. In 2022, he set the franchise record with 17 rushing touchdowns in a season while also accumulating 1,000 yards rushing.

However, his career grinded to a halt when he left Detroit. He managed just 306 rushing yards and one touchdown with the Saints in 2023 (at just 2.9 YPC), then followed it up with 164 rushing yards in 2024. After a year away from the NFL, how much is left in the 31-year-old back?

Do you want the Lions to sign Jamaal Williams ?

My answer: The heart and the reporter side of me says emphatically yes. Williams was a character and a joy to chop it up with in the locker room. His addition would also make a very good story, and he'd be an endless fountain of good quotes. In short, he'd be good for business.

But as a football analyst, it's hard for me to make a logical case here. While I'd like a more even split between Gibbs and the RB2 to ensure we're still getting the best version of Gibbs in December and January… and in 2029, they have Vaki and Saylors for a reason. They still believe in Vaki as a potential offensive weapon, but he needs the reps and learning experiences. I thought he already made a nice jump from a rough Week 1 to a fairly solid Week 2.

The Lions rostered Vaki and Saylor not just for their special teams acumen, but because they believe in them as depth pieces behind Pacheco. As soon as Pacheco goes down, that doesn't mean they have to completely change course. Trust your depth, and if they struggle or suffer another injury, then we can have a discussion about Williams. But, for now, I don't really see a reason for adding a player who hasn't been productive in the NFL since 2022—regardless of much I may admire him as a person.

What are your thoughts? Vote in the poll below and share your further thoughts in the comment section.

articles.body:
Week 2 of the NFL season reminded us how quickly the NFL card market can turn (see first article below). Strong starts from players like Derrick Henry and Bryce Young boosted enthusiasm, while injuries to Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels immediately cooled buying momentum. Turns out that Williams' injury isn't as bad as it initially appeared, but he's getting roasted on social for his reaction to it. Will a loss of aura dampen his market as much as a serious injury would have?

The injury bug certainly makes us less excited to chase young prospects… like an Achilles tear, it hurts when the value of your card tanks.

They say you can't time the market, but you'd hope to time it better than this… Jaxson Dart's one-of-one Topps Chrome Prem1ere Patch Auto sold for $500,200 just one day before a knee injury that could end his season. The timing adds to a growing trend of injuries cooling enthusiasm for young NFL quarterbacks, reinforcing how quickly six-figure card values can swing before players establish long-term resumes.

eBay is expanding its Authenticity Guarantee to eligible raw U.S. coins over $500 and graded coins, with PCGS handling multi-point physical inspections before shipment. The move comes as coin collecting gains momentum among younger collectors through social media and eBay Live, with collectible coin searches up more than 30% year-over-year. By adding authentication, tamper-proof packaging, and standardized condition guidelines, eBay aims to make high-end coin collecting more trusted and accessible.

The marquee lots are Warhol's Flowers and Lichtenstein's Green Head, each carrying estimates up to $3.5 million. We've talked about Towns' love of collecting here before, but always focused on sports cards. Now we can add fine art to the list.

When the government confiscates an item like this, what happens to the money? Does it go back to the buyer of the meteorite? If anyone knows, holler at us.

articles.title: Ex-Rams QB reportedly linked to Giants after Jaxson Dart injury
articles.summary: The former Rams quarterback could find a new starting role in the NFL in 2026.
articles.body:
Jimmy Garoppolo 's name has resurfaced in NFL circles, and this time it's not connected to the Los Angeles Rams .

The New York Giants are set to be without rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season after he suffered a knee injury, leaving Jameis Winston as the team's starter for the foreseeable future this season. With New York needing to find a way to keep its season afloat, ESPN's Mike Garafolo floated Garoppolo as a realistic option worth watching.

"Jimmy Garoppolo is still out there," Garafolo said. "That's a name. The Rams wanted him back, by the way. He did consider retirement at one point. He has been working out. Retirement's not where the way he'd want to go. He would go for the right situation. My feel is that this would be one of the right situations for Jimmy Garoppolo here. So I would not be surprised if there's some discussion regarding him."

Garoppolo, who'll be 35 in November, spent the past two seasons as the Rams' backup. Despite Sean McVay saying on multiple occasions that Los Angeles would welcome Garoppolo back , the sides never got a deal done in free agency, and the Rams instead moved on with the current quarterback room built around Matthew Stafford , Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett .

Garoppolo also had discussions with the Arizona Cardinals , reportedly with former Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur pushing to bring him to the desert, but that deal fell apart before Arizona's own quarterback situation was even resolved. Garoppolo reportedly considered retirement earlier this offseason but has continued working out and would be open to playing again in the right spot.

With the Giants suddenly needing a more viable starter ahead of Winston, and Garoppolo sitting unsigned in late September, it's not hard to see why his name is back in the conversation.

articles.title: Trinidad Chambliss Is The Best QB In College Football. What's His NFL Draft Ceiling?
articles.summary: Trinidad Chambliss is the early Heisman favorite. But with his size and age complicating his NFL draft stock, Rob Rang grades the Ole Miss QB in five scouting categories.
articles.body: With all due respect to Arch Manning, Dante Moore and so many other celebrated quarterbacks throughout the college football landscape, the most impressive player at the position through the first month of the season has been Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss. In guiding the Rebels to a 3-0 start while completing 70% of his passes for 924 yards and seven touchdowns (as well as rushing for 64 yards and two more scores), Chambliss has catapulted ahead of his peers to emerge as the current favorite to win the Heisman Trophy. While some of the other QBs of the 2027 class have fizzled under the brightest lights, Chambliss has consistently excelled, turning skeptics of his pro prospects into believers. But there are undoubtedly still doubters. And it boils down to two factors: His size (he's listed at 6-foot-0) and his age (he recently turned 24). There are five categories I’ve long used to scout quarterbacks: accuracy, anticipation, arm talent, athleticism and attitude. I call them the five A’s of quarterback evaluation. After diving into the 2026 tape, I broke down and graded Chambliss in each category. 1.Accuracy Whether it be analysts, NFL scouts, coaches or fans, it never ceases to amaze me how often folks fall for a quarterback with brilliant athletic tools but subpar accuracy. Plain and simple, accuracy is the single most important element when evaluating a QB. The ball needs to hit receivers in stride to help them create after the catch. Spin rate, velocity and touch are also important, but not as critical as being able to thread the needle from various distances and trajectories. Fortunately for Chambliss, this is one of his many strengths. The super senior routinely fires lasers while flat-footed in the pocket. Even better, he might be even more accurate on the move, as this strike shows. This isn’t to suggest that Chambliss is automatic. During the early part of last season, his first at Ole Miss following four at Division II Ferris State, too many of his deep balls had a tendency to float. Chambliss is good but not great at layering passes between the second and third levels of the defense. Throwing the ball with enough loft to lift it over linebackers and drop it in front of the safeties is critical in today’s NFL, and it will be a departure from the relatively simple offense he’s running with the Rebels. Grade: B+ 2.Anticipation Pardon the cliché, but the game just seems to come so easily for Chambliss. He’s a natural with impressive instincts and poise and he can improvise. He has enough arm strength (more on this later) to zip the ball past defenders after his receivers have gained clearance, but he’s at his best when anticipating their breaks and starting his delivery before they’ve made their final cut to get open. I think this is clearest when Chambliss surveys the field from a clean pocket. He shows impressive field vision — especially for a shorter quarterback — efficiently working through his progressions and speeding up his release when needed. Again, there were some worrisome throws early in his time at Ole Miss in which he either stared down his primary read or failed to account for multiple defenders. And while he was not intercepted by Miami in the Fiesta Bowl last season, he got away with some questionable decisions. Grade: B+ 3.Arm Talent There is no getting around it: At the highest level, quarterbacks sometimes just have to sling it past defenders. The openings can be so minuscule that big-time velocity is required. Chambliss has that type of arm strength. While the breakaway speed by his teammate, Deuce Alexander, is also worth noting on the play below, the throw is an absolute dart. Or this touchdown strike last weekend against LSU. As mentioned earlier, Chambliss put a little too much air under some of his previous deep balls at Ole Miss but this year he’s throwing the ball with greater touch and accuracy. This throw travels nearly 40 yards in the air and is perfectly placed where only his receiver can get it. Grade: A- 4.Athleticism This is a tricky category when evaluating quarterbacks because scouts are prioritizing pocket mobility, flexibility and the strength to fight through arm tackles rather than the pure explosive athleticism indicated in 40-yard dash times or vertical jumps. Chambliss has agility and creativity as a scrambler, but he’s not a dynamic runner warranting comparisons to Lamar Jackson or Kyler Murray. He’s posted impressive rushing totals in his 16 starts at Ole Miss, including 591 yards and 10 scores, but I don’t expect him to wow in pre-draft workouts and wouldn’t be surprised at all if he opts not to run prior to the draft. Given his statistics, I was actually a bit disappointed in Chambliss’ pure athleticism. He’s alert and will take yardage when given to him, but I was surprised by how many times he struggled to escape the pocket with backside pursuit often getting home. He’s more elusive than explosive. Granted, some of the best scrambling quarterbacks in the NFL aren’t necessarily elite athletes. No one would call Brock Purdy as athletic as Jackson, for example, but opponents rarely get a clean hit on him, and he’s run for 12 touchdowns over 51 NFL games. Over that same span, Jackson has 13 rushing touchdowns. While Chambliss isn't the most explosive dual-threat quarterback of the 2027 draft, he’s very effective. Grade: B- 5.Attitude Certain leadership qualities are expected at the quarterback position. Ideally, quarterbacks have the confident demeanor that can lift the spirits of teammates without becoming an egomaniac. As a former under-recruited prospect who began his college career as a backup at Ferris State, Chambliss should have perspective. Since that time, of course, Chambliss won a national championship at Ferris State before transferring to Mississippi, where he’s become a household name while winning 14 of his 16 starts and turning the Rebels into a top-10 program. For all of his impressive physical skills, what scouts appreciate most about Chambliss is the fact that the moment doesn’t ever seem too big for him. His championship pedigree and clutch play late in ball games have scouts excited about the impact that he might have on their own NFL teams. Grade: A The Bottom Line Like with most young quarterbacks, Chambliss can improve his throwing mechanics and decision-making, but he obviously cannot do anything about his height or age. He is undeniably older than scouts would prefer, and his below-average height does show up on tape with Chambliss occasionally missing reads. While short, the 210-pound Chambliss has a muscular, compact frame and is similar in stature to former No. 1 overall pick Baker Mayfield and 10-time Pro Bowler Russell Wilson. Because of their size, some questioned if they would remain healthy in the NFL, despite proving durable at the high school and collegiate levels, as Chambliss has to this point. It's perhaps worth noting that Mayfield and Wilson have combined to miss a grand total of five games to injury over their respective NFL careers — a span that includes 23 seasons and more than 300 contests. Unless medical testing at the Scouting Combine unearths some previously unknown issue with Chambliss, I see no reason why NFL teams should worry about his durability. And given how long quarterbacks are playing in today’s NFL, his age also shouldn’t be a huge concern. In fact, I think it should be viewed as a positive: He'll enter the NFL with more perspective and maturity than most quarterbacks. Now, is Chambliss a surefire first-round selection? A lot can change between September and April. But if the NFL draft were today, he wouldn’t just be a first-round pick. Chambliss might be the first quarterback to come off the board.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' jaw-dropping 8-acre Missouri estate features a private football field, golf hole and swim-up bar most NFL stars can only dream of
articles.summary: For Patrick Mahomes, home is more than a place to unwind after a demanding NFL season.
articles.body: For Patrick Mahomes, home is more than a place to unwind after a demanding NFL season. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has created a personal retreat where football, family life and luxury come together. His sprawling Missouri estate offers something most sports stars can only dream of: a private football field right outside his door. From a basketball court to a resort-style pool, the property reflects Mahomes' vision of life beyond the stadium. It also represents a major personal investment in Kansas City, the city where he chose to build his future.Patrick Mahomes built his dream estate after committing to the ChiefsMahomes purchased the eight-acre property in Belton, Missouri, in September 2020, shortly after signing his landmark 10-year contract extension with Kansas City. Instead of buying a ready-made mansion, he chose to create a home that suited his long-term plans.The custom estate took several years to complete, with construction wrapping up in 2023. In Netflix's Quarterback documentary, Mahomes explained why he decided to build from the ground up."I chose to secure the land and start the construction process when I committed to my contract here in Kansas City. The 10-year extension was a deliberate choice because I was certain about wanting a long-term presence here."He also shared the thinking behind the project, saying, "Given that commitment, I thought, 'Since I'll be here for the foreseeable future, why not construct the exact home I have in mind?'"His decision turned a major career milestone into a lasting family investment. Rather than treating Kansas City as a temporary stop, Mahomes planned a home where he could settle down with his wife, Brittany Mahomes, and their three children.Patrick Mahomes' private football field and luxury amenitiesThe estate's standout feature is a private football field, complete with Mahomes' personal logo at midfield and his surname painted across an end zone. For a quarterback who spends much of the year preparing for NFL games, the field offers a place to throw passes, train and enjoy football on his own terms.But the property goes well beyond the gridiron. Its amenities include an indoor basketball court, a par-3 golf hole, a private pond and a resort-style swimming pool with a swim-up bar. Mahomes also has access to a hotel-inspired fitness centre and spacious outdoor areas designed for entertaining.The setup gives the family plenty of ways to relax without leaving home. It also brings recreation and training into one private space, a rare feature even among professional athletes' properties.Mahomes' Missouri estate is not his only luxury residence. He also owns an offseason home in the exclusive Vaquero golf community in Westlake, Texas. The nearly 7,800-square-foot modern farmhouse includes a wine room, an infinity-edge pool and outdoor entertainment areas.Still, the Belton compound holds particular significance. It reflects Mahomes' commitment to the Chiefs and his desire to put down roots in Kansas City. For the star quarterback, the estate is not simply a display of wealth. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Giants' Possible QB Trade Targets After Jaxson Dart's Knee Injury
articles.summary: With Jaxson Dart set to miss the rest of the season, the New York Giants find themselves in the quarterback market as they try to salvage their 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
With Jaxson Dart set to miss the rest of the season, the New York Giants find themselves in the quarterback market as they try to salvage their 2026 campaign.

Appearing on Thursday's episode of Get Up , ESPN's Adam Schefter cited Gardner Minshew of the Arizona Cardinals and Mac Jones of the San Francisco 49ers as potential targets for the Giants.

Schefter added a trade for Jones would cost "a lot" if the 49ers are even willing to discuss a deal. He also noted the Giants will see how Week 3 with Jameis Winston starting against the Tennessee Titans go before they make any decisions.

Dart will undergo surgery on his knee after being injured on the Giants' first offensive possession in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Taking over after Dart left, Winston did not inspire a lot of confidence with how he played. The former No. 1 overall pick finished 11-of-27 for 111 yards and one interception.

Sunday will mark Winston's first start since Week 12 last season. He hasn't won a game as the starting quarterback since Week 12 of the 2024 season when he led the Cleveland Browns to a 24-19 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In-season quarterback trades are very rare. There have only been three since the start of the 2021 season with Joe Flacco involved in two of them. He was traded to the New York Jets in October 2021 and Cincinnati Bengals in October 2025.

The other one saw Joshua Dobbs traded by the Arizona Cardinals to the Minnesota Vikings in October 2023 after Kirk Cousins tore his Achilles.

Another potential issue for the Giants is it's still so early in the season that teams may not be eager to break up their quarterback room until they have a better understanding of how things look.

San Francisco was reportedly seeking at least a second-round pick for Jones in the offseason. Even though Brock Purdy has played very well to start this season, he has missed time in each of the past two years that the 49ers might not want to part with Jones.

The Cardinals are in a position to potentially capitalize on New York's situation. Minshew is the No. 2 quarterback on their depth chart, but they used a third-round pick in the 2026 draft on Carson Beck.

Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy worked with Minshew last season when they were both with the Kansas City Chiefs.

The schedule is set up for Winston and the Giants to at least tread water for a bit as they assess the quarterback market. Their upcoming games after the Titans on Sunday include the Cardinals in Week 4 and Washington Commanders in Week 5 before back-to-back games against the New Orleans Saints and Houston Texans leading into their bye.

articles.title: New 'Madden' Movie Trailer and Release Date Drops Featuring Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale
articles.summary: Some of the biggest movie stars in Hollywood are coming together to remember the legendary career of John Madden.
articles.body:
Some of the biggest movie stars in Hollywood are coming together to remember the legendary career of John Madden.

Amazon MGM Studios released the first official trailer for the upcoming biopic entitled Madden on Thursday. The movie stars Academy Award winner Nicolas Cage as the title character, as well as Academy Award winner Christian Bale as Al Davis.

The movie is directed by David O. Russell and also features Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller, John Mulaney and Shane Gillis.

This comes after Prime Video released a teaser for the film, which will be released on Nov. 18, that included Cage explaining what it was like to portray Madden:

" Madden is the celebration of a brilliant mind whose once in a century spirit and personality, partnership with his daring wife Virginia, lifelong friendships, and infectious love of people and football transcended the world of sports," the press release read.

The story of football is not complete without Madden.

He was a Hall of Fame coach for the Oakland Raiders for 10 seasons, finishing with a 103-32-7 record and a Super Bowl title. The Raiders reached the playoffs in all but two of his seasons at the helm as he and Davis built a dominant team that helped define a generation.

Madden did far more than reach the Hall of Fame as a coach, though, as he became one of the most iconic broadcasters in sports history and also inspired EA Sports' famous Madden video game that remains a key part of the cultural zeitgeist today.

While Madden died in 2021 at 85 years old, he remains one of the most important and influential people in the history of sports.

And the movie will look to capture some of that famous life and his football journey.

articles.title: Jaxson Dart and Jayden Daniels face uncertain NFL futures after latest injury blows, says Phoebe Schecter
articles.summary: What will Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury mean for him and John Harbaugh's New York Giants? And what next for the Washington Commanders and Jayden Daniels?; listen to Inside the Huddle podcast with Neil Reynolds, Phoebe Schecter and Jeff Reinebold throughout the 2026 NFL season
articles.body:
Dart was ruled out for the remainder of the season this week after suffering a knee injury on the first drive of Monday night's defeat to the Los Angeles Rams.

A day earlier Daniels was forced off when he dislocated his left elbow in Washington's defeat to the Dallas Cowboys, having missed 10 games last season.

Their absence could yet see to both teams finding themselves in position to target another quarterback at next year's NFL Draft.

"It is something to watch," Schecter said of their uncertain future on Inside the Huddle. "And I think what's so unique about all of that the implications are so much bigger, right?

"There's a high chance with this happening to both quarterbacks that they could end up picking first when it comes to a draft and who you're looking at - you're probably looking at a quarterback. So how does that relationship work?

"Because you've got two young quarterbacks as your starting quarterbacks. Are you saying you don't believe in them? Do they become the Sam Darnolds of the world and then they go on to just be travellers among the teams? What does that mean for the other teams who actually need a quarterback who keep missing out on these opportunities?

"It's kind of this incredible butterfly effect, knock on ultimately that could happen."

The Giants had cut a reinvigorated figure after starting life under first-year head coach John Harbaugh with a statement win over the Dallas Cowboys, Dart seemingly spearheading an exciting new chapter for a young New York team.

That excitement was swiftly and ruthlessly dashed on Monday, veteran Jameis Winston now set to take the reins under center.

According to ESPN stats, Dart, wide receiver Malik Nabers and running back Cam Skattebo have only shared the field for 3.5 per cent of the Giants' offensive plays over the last two seasons, equating to 43 of 1,208.

"Jaxson Dart plays a certain way that he puts himself in harm's way," said Neil Reynolds. "Now, that's not what happened with the injury, ironically this time, but he is a regular visitor to the Blue Tent.

"And Jayden Daniels, we still have those questions about whether he's built to withstand this, so I don't think anyone would question their skill, but can have all the skill in the world. It does you no good if you're on the sideline for nine games every season.

"We haven't had a Super Bowl yet [which has been] kind of ruined at the last minute by a backup coming in. Now Nick Foles had to come off the bench to lead Philadelphia, but we've had a couple of championship games now where they've been completely taken over by a backup quarterback story.

"Jarrett Stidham last year with the Denver Broncos, Brock Purdy went down for the San Francisco 49ers. So the NFL is losing its biggest stars. We want Caleb Williams on the field. We want Jayden Daniels on the field."

Chicago Bears quarterback Williams was another major casualty on Sunday as he was carted off with a hamstring injury in his side's 9-3 defeat to the Minnesota Vikings. Backup Tyson Bagent has meanwhile been placed in the concussion protocol, meaning 38-year-old Case Keenum could start for the Bears against the Eagles in Monday Night Football.

"Now you're going to your third string quarterback and you know, [head coach] Ben Johnson said it's open to anybody, but there is no sport without having a starting quarterback," Schecter continued.

"They've brought in more and more rules to try and protect the quarterback, but this isn't even about that. These are just kind of freak odd accidents that are happening.

"With Jayden Daniels he's a very small-framed person. And that's part of what makes him so good at what he does. But it's also a bit of a concern. I almost think why wouldn't you have just worn a brace knowing that it dislocated already

"There's way more questions, but also look at our first two weeks of the season. We're missing four starting quarterbacks already."

articles.title: Falcons vs. Packers 'Thursday Night Football' betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper break downs his favorite bets in the Falcons-Packers matchup on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
Things will heat up under the bright lights at Lambeau Field on Thursday when the Green Bay Packers (1-1) host the winless Atlanta Falcons (0-2) in a crucial matchup for both franchises.

The Packers have struggled on both sides of the ball, suffering a 39-22 loss against Minnesota in their season opener before needing overtime to fend off the New York Jets in a 20-17 win this past Sunday.

As for their foes, things couldn't be going much worse. The Falcons, who dropped a 20-13 road decision against Pittsburgh in Week 1, were handed a 34-3 blowout defeat against Carolina in their Week 2 home opener.

Here are a few wagers I like on Thursday night.

Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers (-5, 43.5)

This game opened with Green Bay as a 7.5-point favorite, but heavy money started pouring in on Atlanta when it was announced quarterback Michael Penix Jr. would make his first start of the season after tearing his left ACL in Week 11 a year ago.

My guess is we will see the late public money come in on the Packers throughout the day Thursday. However, I like the winless Falcons to keep this one close and potentially spring a big upset.

Here are some interesting data points for Atlanta backers:

Teams starting 0-2 straight up and against the spread are 30-12 ATS (71.4%) in Week 3 as underdogs dating back to 2015.

Teams that begin 0-2 are 40-17-1 ATS (70.2%) facing 1-1 opponents since 2010.

Since 1980, only 12% of teams starting 0-2 have made the playoffs.

Kevin Stefanski is a perfect 5-0 in Thursday night games, so we should have a determined, motivated Atlanta team believing it can pull off the Thursday night shocker.

The return of Penix also means someone competent will be under center to get the ball to do-it-all running back Bijan Robinson , as well as wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts . Atlanta has a dismal 23.1% third-down conversion rate so far, but I'm expecting we'll see this number will start to improve with No. 9 back calling the shots.

With that in mind, I'm parlaying Atlanta to cover the spread and the total staying under the points at slightly higher numbers to get us into a plus-money wager.

Both offenses struggled last week moving the ball and I don't see either fixing its issues four days removed from those games. Expect a tight affair and this one to be decided late.

Bet: Same Game Parlay with alternate lines: Falcons +7.5 and under 46.5 (+135, FanDuel)

WR Christian Watson over 4.5 receptions (-138, FanDuel)

If there has been one bright spot for the Green Bay offense thus far, it has been Watson.

Through two games, the Packers standout finds himself ranked seventh in the NFL in total targets (19), with 11 coming in Sunday's squeaker against the Jets. In the season opener, Watson finished with six catches for 148 yards and two touchdowns in defeat.

Combine those stats with the fact that Green Bay is facing a team that just let Carolina quarterback Bryce Young torch it for 287 and three touchdown passes, and Watson is primed for another monster outing.

Love is going to have to get the ball out quickly to his cast of receivers, since his offensive line couldn't be in any worse shape. Injuries galore have beset Green Bay, with right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele as the latest fallen lineman to be deemed out for the season.

With an Atlanta defense that will consistently try to pressure Love, I fully expect Watson to be the popular target via shorter routes. Veteran Atlanta cornerback A.J. Terrell was placed on the IR this week with a groin injury, which gives me even more confidence Watson will be on Love's radar — and open — throughout the night.

TE Kyle Pitts over 37.5 receiving yards (-114, FanDuel)

To say it has been a disappointing start to the season for Pitts would be an understatement.

Pitts, who earned second-team All-Pro honors last season after hauling in 88 catches for 928 yards and five touchdowns, has just one reception for 15 years through two games. Mind you, Pitts had quarterbacks Cooper Rush and Jack Strand running the offense, so I'm cutting him some major slack.

With Penix back, I fully expect we see the usually busy version of Pitts, who became the NFL's third highest-paid tight end in the offseason via a three-year deal worth $54 million.

Pitts cleared this number in six of nine games last season when Penix started, so we know the sixth-year pro is one of his favorite go-to guys. And the statistics back it up, with Pitts racking up 30 receptions on 38 targets in those six contests.

In the season opener, Minnesota tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver combined for six catches for 58 yards and a touchdown. Pitts is better than both — and any tight end that the Jets sent out against the Packers — so we should see a big night from him.

Our Monday angle was that tight end Terrance Ferguson would pick up the slack for the Los Angeles Rams when Puka Nacua would miss the clash with the New York Giants .

Needless to say, Ferguson delivered for his backers with six catches for 54 yards and a touchdown.

Last Thursday, we targeted fellow tight ends Sam LaPorta ( Detroit ) and Dalton Kincaid (Buffalo) to score in that showdown. And both found the end zone to help us sweep those picks.

Fast forward to Thursday's showdown and we have a prime spot for another tight end to shine. The Packers will be without the services of wide receiver Jayden Reed , who suffered a neck injury against the Jets and will miss a substantial amount of time. That creates a massive hole in an offense still trying to find its identity.

Suffice it to say, this is a perfect spot for Kraft to become a focal point of the Green Bay aerial attack and recreate the success he enjoyed last season (44 catches for 489 yards and six touchdowns) in just eight games after suffering an ACL tear in a Nov. 2 loss against Carolina.

Kraft is coming off a game where he played 98% of the offensive snaps and now faces an Atlanta defense that has already yielded three touchdowns to tight ends this season.

Piggybacking on my insight in regard to the betting angle on his receiving yards, I like Pitts to get into the end zone, as well. With Robinson and London garnering the majority of the offensive attention, the 6-foot-6 tight end should be able to feast on some mismatches with the smaller Green Bay linebackers and secondary unit.

And to get this wager at this price is just too good to pass up in this spot.

articles.body: The first two games saw more injuries than expected, which is especially concerning as mid-season and crucial games begin. The New York Giants lost Jaxson Dart to an MCL, PCL, and meniscus injury that requires surgery.The Los Angeles Rams played Week 2 against the Giants without Puka Nacua because he developed a new injury, which head coach Sean McVay compared to “pre-hernia” pain.Baltimore Ravens’ wide receiver Zay Flowers first hurt his hamstring during a joint practice on August 20. Although he seemed fine for the regular season, his hamstring injury flared up during the Week 1 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, and he has not practiced fully since then.Additionally, the New Orleans Saints signed Travis Etienne Jr. to a blockbuster, four-year, $48 million contract this offseason, but he has not yet scored a touchdown through the first two games of the 2026 NFL season.He has appeared on the team’s injury report for the first time ahead of their Week 3 clash against the Las Vegas Raiders, dealing with a nagging hamstring injury.Jaxson Dart ruled out for regular season but could return for playoffsNFL Insider Ian Rapoport said just hours ago on Good Morning Football that the New York Giants QB Jaxson Dart could make a playoff appearance - provided the Giants make it and his recovery goes well.“Jaxson Dart is going to be out for the regular season, having surgery on his knee that, of course, we saw he injured on Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams,” Rapoport said.“Initial thought was it was not a major injury. Then they had the MRI, and all optimism went away. It is a torn meniscus. It is an injury to his MCL. My understanding is Jaxson Dart will have surgery to repair both of them. Colleague Adam Schefter also adds there is damage to the PCL as well.Now, the meniscus is essentially the longest recovery. So that is four to six weeks, really five to six weeks. So we will see when Jaxson Dart is able to recover.The Giants kept the door open for a possible playoff run. Maybe he could make a late appearance. We shall see. That would mean everything had gone incredibly, incredibly well.”Jaxson Dart was sandwiched between two Los Angeles Rams defenders, Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart, after attempting a third-and-8 pass. He took a hard hit to his left knee, stayed on the ground, and grabbed his leg.After receiving medical attention, he walked to the medical tent for evaluation and was seen limping as he headed to the locker room.X-rays were negative, but an MRI revealed that his meniscus, MCL, and PCL were damaged. He will undergo surgery and is declared out for the season. Veteran quarterback Jameis Winston will take over as the starter for the New York Giants.Puka Nacua could sit out Week 3 clash against DenverDuring an ESPN Los Angeles interview, Rams head coach Sean McVay opened up about Puka Nacua’s progress and potential Week 3 return.“We’ll see,” McVay said. “It doesn’t… You know, he’s not making great progress. But we’d love to welcome Puka back with open arms. If not, I’ve got a ton of confidence in the group we will go with if he doesn’t go.”Puka Nacua missed training camp and the preseason practice schedule with a core muscle injury. He played in the Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, but he missed practice last week because of a new injury - hip and groin soreness.He also missed the Week 2 win over the New York Giants due to this hip and groin soreness, and he could miss the Week 3 clash against the Denver Broncos as well.Puka Nacua was a non-participant in Wednesday’s jog-through.
