articles.title: Week 3 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Ravens set for a great matchup in Brazil
articles.summary: The Ravens and Cowboys both come into Week 3 with 1-1 records.
articles.body:
The NFL is investing a lot into its international series, which is clear from this week's matchup in Brazil.

The league's most marketable team, the Dallas Cowboys , gets to face a Baltimore Ravens team that has Super Bowl hopes and one of the most marketable players in Lamar Jackson . It's a great matchup for Rio de Janeiro. The NFL booked some top-tier matchups for other countries this season, and this might be the best of the group.

The fear is the turf at Maracanã Stadium. There was enough concern that the NFL's field director commented on it this week to ESPN and said the league isn't concerned. That doesn't mean it will be a perfect surface or close to it. There has been a lot of rain in Rio de Janeiro over the past six weeks and soccer players have complained about the turf. For two fast offenses, that could be a big factor.

The Cowboys defense could use the help. Dallas looked better in Week 2, but still allowed 389 yards even though Washington lost Jayden Daniels on the final play of the first half. The offense will be good, though maybe not quite as good if the turf in Brazil is poor. It's the defense Dallas needs to worry about.

There is some concern about the Ravens' offense if receiver Zay Flowers can't play through a hamstring injury, and Baltimore will surely be careful if the turf is bad. But Jackson will make it work against a Dallas defense that is still suspect. The Cowboys' defensive issues are the main reason why Ravens -3.5 is the pick. Hopefully the conditions in Brazil don't bother what looks like a phenomenal matchup on Sunday.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 3 of the NFL season:

It's not fun to pick the Packers right now. They're beat up on offense, especially the offensive line. That's a reason this line moved down from Packers -7.5. But it's not like the Falcons are good. Sure, getting Michael Penix Jr. back helps. But Penix hasn't been great in his career and he's playing his first game action since Nov. 16, 2025. It's hard to have a lot of trust in him or the Falcons.

It's not too surprising the Jaguars faded in the second half last week at Denver . Playing in altitude early in the season is not easy. The Jaguars are a good team. Are the Patriots? Probably, but staying in their offensive funk last week against the Steelers wasn't promising. The Jaguars look like the better team.

Teams using their backup quarterback often get a short-term bump. And while Jameis Winston has his flaws and didn't look good on Monday night, he is one of the NFL's more capable backups. While the Titans did play well against the Eagles last week, I'm not convinced they've turned a corner.

If you've followed these picks over the years, you haven't seen many double-digit road favorites being the pick. Teams facing the 2026 Dolphins might be an exception. The Dolphins haven't shown anything yet that would make anyone believe they are going to be competitive in many games this season. Maybe the Dolphins get a jolt in their home opener, but it's not a team that's showing any signs of life yet.

Speaking of teams that haven't shown anything yet, the Steelers are 1-1 and are lucky they played the Falcons in Week 1. There are two teams that have just one offensive touchdown this season: Pittsburgh and Atlanta . The Falcons have the excuse that they were down to their third- and then fourth-string quarterbacks. The Steelers have mostly used their preferred lineup. They just haven't been very good. The Bengals offense hasn't heated up yet, but it will, and the defense looks greatly improved. Dexter Lawrence II is a fun dark horse NFL Defensive Player of the Year candidate.

The last time we saw this matchup in Landover, Md., the Seahawks blew out the Commanders 38-14 last season. And Jayden Daniels played most of that game before dislocating his elbow. Daniels is probably going to miss this week after dislocating his elbow again, and the Seahawks defense looks like it might be even better than last season. So why pick a Marcus Mariota-led Commanders team to cover? Ugly dogs cover all the time in the NFL, and you won't know many people picking Washington here.

If there are any signs of life in the Chargers this season, we'll see it Sunday. They've been awful. But this line first opened at Bills -3 and jumped up four points the last couple weeks. It's justified based on how both teams have looked so far. But it is also a reminder that the full touchdown is a lot. The Chargers are entering an excruciating part of their schedule and have to know that it's now or never if they're going to save their season.

Maybe what we saw from Deshaun Watson last week was a sign that he'll be just fine as Browns quarterback. It seems more like the Buccaneers defense was that bad in the second half. If Watson does it again, hats off to him. The Panthers have gotten off to a hot start, and part of that is playing the Bears' and Falcons' defenses. But don't forget how Jacksonville torched the Browns' defense in Week 1. Bryce Young might keep his good start going.

I'm 0-2 in trusting Houston this season, but undeterred. Houston will play well this season. The defense was very good last week, but the offense wasn't. That should change against a Colts defense that has given up 1,029 yards (!!!) in two games.

The Jets haven't been bad this season. They just couldn't finish last week against the Packers. And the Lions defense looks like it might keep every opponent in the game. Even if the Lions look good here, the defense allowing a backdoor cover will stay in play.

Get ready to handle the blitz, Buccaneers. The Vikings and their defensive coordinator Brian Flores are blitzing on over 80% of opponents' dropbacks so far this season. And it's working. But this is just the time when a 2-0 Vikings team is favored on the road against an 0-2 Buccaneers team and it looks so easy to pick Minnesota . The Buccaneers are the more desperate team and got embarrassed last week losing to the Browns, and unless you believe they have given up on Todd Bowles already, that's generally the type of team worth backing.

Maybe the Chargers are simply putrid. But don't forget that in Week 1, the Cardinals were a 9.5-point underdog against the Chargers and went on the road and won. It's doubtful that they're beating the 49ers straight up, but as long as they're not facing the Seahawks defense they should be able to move the ball.

This point spread might be too little respect for the Saints, or a lot for the Raiders. The Saints are a missed two-point conversion away from beating the Lions and Ravens on the road to start the season. They might be good. The Raiders are much improved too. Picking the Saints isn't necessarily a fade of the Raiders, but acknowledging how impressive New Orleans ' start has been.

The Broncos have played two good quarters out of eight. The Rams were a no-show in Week 1, but as they were pounding the Giants in Week 2 it sure looked like we can excuse that performance to a weird Australia trip and weirder travel plan for it. Part of that travel plan was presumably to not be impacted through September by jet lag, and that might have worked. Historically, the Broncos are good at home in September and they're not a bad team. But maybe what we saw Monday night was the first sign of the Rams being the team they were hyped up to be before the season.

It's hard to know if Caleb Williams will play. If he does, then Bears +4.5 is an easy play. But the Bears could be down to Case Keenum against a talented Eagles defense. And if Williams does play, will he be fully mobile with his hamstring injury? The safe play is to take the Eagles, though they have not been impressive despite a 2-0 start.

articles.title: Puka Nacua 'not making great progress,' according to Rams coach Sean McVay
articles.summary: Nacua missed Week 2 with groin soreness and could miss Sunday night's matchup against the Broncos.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are likely to be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for a second straight week, judging by head coach Sean McVay's comments on Wednesday.

"We'll see," McVay told ESPN Los Angeles . "He's not making great progress. But we'll welcome Puka back with open arms, but if not I've got a ton of confidence in the group that we will go with if he doesn't go."

Nacua missed the Rams' Monday night win over the New York Giants with what was listed as a hip injury, but McVay said the wideout had "a little bit of soreness" in his groin.

Earlier in the day, McVay said he wasn't sure if Nacua would play Sunday night against the Denver Broncos, adding that the injury is not a long-term concern for the team and they are just being cautious.

"When you're a skill player and you're really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up and you feel just ... it's like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is kind of what he's feeling," McVay said . "And so you err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward."

What Nacua is dealing with now is not related to the psoas issue that caused him to miss time during training camp. He was healthy enough to play Week 1 during the Rams' loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Nacua caught five passes on nine targets for 74 yards.

The Rams held a walk-through on Wednesday, but the expectation was that Nacua would not have practiced.

"We all want him to be able to be out there, but we want him to be able to return to performance, not just be able to just kind of gut through it," McVay said.

articles.title: Kyle Long reveals how NFL pressure, injuries and depression took a heavy toll and why therapy became a turning point
articles.summary: Former Chicago Bears guard Kyle Long is speaking openly about anxiety and depression during his NFL career, including a difficult day at training camp
articles.body: Former Chicago Bears guard Kyle Long is speaking openly about anxiety and depression during his NFL career, including a difficult day at training camp when he felt unable to leave the team bus. In an interview with PEOPLE, he said therapy, honest conversations and support from people close to him helped him understand what was happening. Long is now sharing his experience through Johnson & Johnson’s Generation Fine campaign.Kyle Long opens up about depression during his NFL careerLong said his mental health struggles may have started when he was young. He had trouble explaining how he felt and believed it was simply part of growing up. After entering the NFL, playing pressure, injuries and losing games brought stronger fear, stress and anxiety.“That’s when it became tangible stress, fear and anxiety,” Long told PEOPLE. “And then you start losing games and you start to really sink into that depression. It becomes something that, in the moment, feels like you’re the only person on the planet who’s dealing with it.”Long spoke with his father, Hall of Famer Howie Long, and brother Chris Long. Still, Long felt he had to handle his problems and keep going.That became harder during the 2015-16 preseason. He was dealing with an injury and the pressure of being one of the older players. He said players were expected to stay composed even when struggling.“One day at training camp, we were on our way back from practice and I just could not get off of the bus to go back to the hotel,” Long recalled. “It just felt like I had a truck on top of me and I couldn’t move.”Kyle Long says therapy changed how he manages anxiety and depressionThat day changed his view of his mental health. He was encouraged to look around the locker room and think about what his teammates might also be facing away from football. He realized he was not alone and needed to take his mental health seriously.Long says therapy and openness have helped him manage anxiety and depression over time. He also learned to seek medical help instead of simply pushing through his feelings.“I am in a constant ‘working on it’ phase,” he told PEOPLE. “You lift weights, you run sprints, you eat healthy, you get eight hours of sleep, you go see a physical therapist. For me, that missing thing was speaking with a medical professional and finding out why I’m feeling the way that I’m feeling, and then knowing that ‘fine’ is not the finish line.”Long is now a studio analyst on CBS Sports’ The NFL Today, joining the show in 2026. He is also working with Johnson & Johnson’s Generation Fine campaign, which encourages people to look beyond simply saying they are “fine.”Johnson & Johnson said in May that Long had battled depression at different stages of his life, including during his NFL career. The company said the campaign encourages conversations with healthcare providers. articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Michael Penix Jr. returns for Falcons, who face similarly desperate Packers
articles.summary: The Falcons are 0-2 and the Packers are 1-1 coming into their Thursday night matchup.
articles.body:
Near the end of the season, some teams are so injured that their lineups don't resemble anything from the beginning of the season.

For the Atlanta Falcons and Green Bay Packers , who face off on Thursday night, those injury problems set in as soon as the season started.

The Falcons are off to a 0-2 start. Their top two quarterbacks, Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa , missed both games. Cooper Rush did not play well when forced into action. Penix, who tore his ACL late last season, will return Thursday. But the Falcons are still missing other players like 2025 first-round pick Jalon Walker .

Still, simply having Penix back will allow the Falcons to get a more realistic view of what their team will be this season. The offense was not functional for two weeks. Their team passer rating is a league-worst 38.2, which is hard to believe. The passer rating if a quarterback threw incomplete every down is 39.6. Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. are talented pass catchers who have been almost invisible this season in a wretched offense. Penix has a lot to prove after two uneven seasons. But compared to what the Falcons had at quarterback through two weeks, he'll be a massive upgrade.

The Packers have their own issues. They were so banged up on the offensive line last week, they had to consider playing tight end Tucker Kraft at tackle during the game. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele is done for the season with a knee injury. Guard Aaron Banks will miss Week 3, as will receiver Jayden Reed . Star pass rusher Micah Parsons won't make his season debut until October. The Packers' offense struggled last week against the Jets, with the running game being a non-factor ( Josh Jacobs is still on the commissioner's exempt list) and Jordan Love throwing for 145 yards. Everything was labored because the decimated offensive line couldn't block.

The Falcons finished last season strong and the Packers were a playoff team. They each had high hopes for this season, but are in scramble mode early on.

Both teams are pretty desperate. But the Packers probably need a win a little more. An 0-3 start would be awful for the Falcons, but they're still in the NFC South. It won't take a great record to be in the race. The Packers are 1-1, but the win wasn't too impressive, needing overtime to beat the Jets. A loss to a reeling Falcons team at home would not be good, especially in what should be a competitive NFC North. A loss would put either team in a bit of a hole early in the season, but the panic around the Packers would ramp up with a loss as a home favorite on Thursday night.

Golden was a 2025 first-round pick who finished last season well, and has had plenty of opportunity so far. Golden has played more than 84% of the snaps and has run 69 routes with a 26.1% target share, which are all promising marks. Those numbers might tick up just a bit with Reed out indefinitely with a neck injury. Golden has 10 catches for 153 yards, which is solid for two games, but it feels like there are some bigger games coming. Last week, the Falcons gave up 34 points to the Panthers , with Bryce Young throwing for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Golden has a chance to make a big impact.

This game opened at Packers -7.5 in the summer, but was under a touchdown on the lookahead lines and is now down to Green Bay -4.5 due to a combination of Michael Penix Jr. being announced as Atlanta's starter, Green Bay's poor play and some Packers injuries (Reed, Bako-Bewele, Banks, etc.). The Falcons looked utterly pathetic on offense in two games with Cooper Rush at QB, so it's hard to believe Penix won't be a massive upgrade. The betting public is behind Green Bay — difficult to blame them — but I'd hold my nose and look at the under here instead. Green Bay's offense has struggled and I don't believe Penix is fully healthy and has had enough practice time to be able to exploit the Packers' D.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

Maybe you don't remember subscribing to the Atlanta Falcons package, but they're showing in prime time for the next three weeks. Here are three fantasy themes to track as we scout the Falcons at Packers.

1. Can Michael Penix Jr. save the Atlanta offense? The Cooper Rush/Jack Strand ticket has been a nightmare for the Falcons (1 touchdown, 5 picks, 7 sacks, 38.2 rating) and it's sunk the fantasy values of Drake London and Kyle Pitts. Penix has been a mediocre quarterback for two years, but he's specifically clicked with London during his time in the NFL.

2. Who's the best option in the Green Bay backfield? MarShawn Lloyd has averaged just 3.0 yards per carry through two weeks and he lost a key fumble against the Jets. Kaleb Johnson is still largely an unknown, but at least he's managed four yards a pop over his eight attempts. More work could be coming here.

3. Is Tucker Kraft ready for a spike? Kraft had a credible 3-65-0 opener at Minnesota , but was held to 15 yards at New York despite running a route on 32 of 34 Green Bay dropbacks. A muted start was always possible for Kraft after suffering an ACL tear in the middle of 2025, but given how much he's already playing, it's fair to expect the production to start rising.

articles.title: Kyle Juszczyk Fined by NFL for Pretending to Chug a Beer During 49ers' Win vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk apparently took things a little too far in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk apparently took things a little too far in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, the NFL fined Juszczyk $14,926 for engaging in an "offensive demonstration" when he celebrated during the 35-13 victory. Juszczyk has already filed an appeal.

"Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste," the league said.

Schefter pointed out that Juszczyk is nicknamed "Juice" and has been celebrating touchdowns and first downs the exact same way throughout his entire career, but this marks the first time he's been fined. He texted Schefter, "And I don't even drink beer!"

Former NFL star J.J. Watt also came to Juszczyk's defense, tweeting that it should be obvious that he was paying homage to his nickname:

Juszczyk recorded two catches for 27 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphins. His celebration came after he found the end zone in the third quarter. He also helped pave the way for a rushing attack that totaled 95 yards and three touchdowns as the 49ers improved to 2-0.

One of the few true fullbacks in the league, Juszczyk has been selected to the Pro Bowl in 10 straight years. Still, he's making just $3.7 million this year, so he will rightfully appeal the fine and try to keep his money in his pockets.

The 49ers will try to remain undefeated when they face the Arizona Cardinals (1-1) in an NFC West matchup on Sunday.

articles.summary: Juszczyk is appealing the NFL's decision after his touchdown celebration against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
Kyle Juszczyk has reportedly been fined $14,926 for his beer-chugging celebration after scoring a touchdown during the San Francisco 49ers ' 35-13 Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins .

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the NFL's letter to the fullback, whose nickname is "Juice," said, "Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste."

Juszczyk's celebration came following his 6-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter to extend the 49ers' lead to 28-6.

The fine, which falls under the NFL's "Sportsmanship — Unsportsmanlike Conduct" category of violations , has already been appealed by Juszczyk, according to Schefter.

This is the second time this season that Juszczyk has been fined by the NFL. During Week 1, he was docked $20,033 for using his helmet while making a block during San Francisco 's win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia.

As part of the appeal process, Juszczyk will have a hearing with one of the NFL's appeals officers — Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson or James Thrash — who are jointly appointed and paid by the league and the NFLPA. Once the officer makes a decision, the ruling is final and binding.

articles.title: From a $1.75 million school gift to a $3 million hospital donation: How Russell Wilson and Ciara built a foundation around helping children
articles.summary: For Russell Wilson and Ciara, the words “Why not you?” have become closely tied to the work they do for children and families.
articles.body: For Russell Wilson and Ciara, the words “Why not you?” have become closely tied to the work they do for children and families. Through the Why Not You Foundation, which they started in 2014, the couple has supported education, children’s health and efforts to fight hunger. The foundation said in 2023 that its partnerships had helped raise more than $13 million for these causes. Since then, its work has continued with several large donations and community programs.How Russell Wilson and Ciara built the Why Not You Foundation around childrenThe idea behind the foundation came from a message Wilson learned from his father, Harrison Wilson III, who encouraged him to believe that he could achieve his goals even when others doubted him. Wilson later carried that message into his charity work, with the foundation focusing on giving young people better access to education, health care and basic support.Wilson had already been spending time with children at Seattle Children’s Hospital before the foundation was created. His visits became a regular part of his life, and his connection with young patients later became an important part of the foundation’s work. The foundation has also supported pediatric cancer research and programs aimed at helping families facing food insecurity.Education has been another major part of their work. In 2020, the Why Not You Foundation committed about $1.75 million to help rebrand and support Cascade Midway Academy, a charter school south of Seattle. The school later became Why Not You Academy and opened to high school students, with a focus on personalized learning, mentorship and work-based opportunities.The couple has also taken their work into communities where they have lived and worked. In 2023, through a partnership with CommonSpirit Health, the foundation helped provide $1 million in grants to 10 organizations in Colorado and Utah. Each group received $100,000 for work involving areas such as education, health equity, food security and support for children and young people.From a Seattle school to major gifts for children’s health and hungerThe foundation’s more recent donations show that its work has expanded beyond education. In November 2025, the Why Not You Foundation announced a $3 million gift to Mount Sinai Kravis Children’s Hospital in New York. The money is supporting two therapeutic spaces, including a Child Life Zone Theater and a play space for children receiving cancer and blood disease care.Just a month later, the foundation announced another $500,000 donation to the Atlanta Community Food Bank and ATL Cares. According to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, the money was expected to help provide more than one million meals to families dealing with food insecurity.In February 2026, the foundation announced a $2 million donation to the Los Cabos Children’s Foundation in Mexico. The gift is being used to expand health and rehabilitation services for children and families in Baja California Sur.Their fundraising efforts have also reached large numbers. In 2025, the Youth Athlete of the Year competition raised $21.66 million, with the money set to support both the Why Not You Foundation and the V Foundation for Cancer Research.The foundation now also runs Why Not You Centers, which are designed to give young people access to mentorship, academic support, creative programs and other resources. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers hints at coaching friction after offensive struggles
articles.summary: After Pittsburgh's offensive struggles continued, quarterback Aaron Rodgers signaled growing friction with the coaching staff over play-calling.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves navigating a delicate situation early in the season, as veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers begins publicly challenging the team's offensive direction. Following a frustrating offensive output, growing friction between the four-time MVP and Pittsburgh's coaching staff has quickly shifted from an internal operational detail to a major national narrative.

Rather than downplaying the communication disconnect on the sideline, Rodgers raised eyebrows by publicly asserting that he needs to take a far more aggressive, hands-on role in overriding play calls he deems ineffective. Will Compton , Taylor Lewan , Delanie Walker , and Clay Matthews , hosts of the " Bussin' with the Boys " podcast, addressed Rodgers recent comments. Lewan, a three-time Pro Bowler, highlighted the rare nature of the veteran quarterback's blunt commentary.

" Steelers in a weird spot," noted Lewan. "Aaron Rodgers sitting there saying like, 'I have to be more upfront with the coaching staff to tell a bad play.' That's a crazy thing to say."

The reaction from his co-hosts was immediate shock, with Lewan noting it ranked in the "probably top five" craziest statements he had heard a starting quarterback make regarding his coaching staff.

The friction isn't limited to internal play-calling loops; Rodgers has also displayed a noticeably sharper edge when fielding questions from beat reporters. However, Compton believes that may work in Rodgers' favor.

As Compton pointed out, "A-Rod is already getting abrasive with the media. They're asking about receivers. I like where he's at. F*** the touches, he's going to be fine."

For a Pittsburgh offense struggling to establish a steady rhythm across the board, a vocal disconnect between its star quarterback and the sideline creates serious operational hurdles. While veteran leaders often push for schematic autonomy, airing those grievances publicly signals that the offense's week-to-week communication remains severely off-track.

If the Steelers hope to salvage their offensive potential, aligning Rodgers and the coaching staff on play selection is paramount. Until those communication breakdowns are resolved behind closed doors, Pittsburgh's offense risks remaining a volatile work in progress.

articles.title: NFL viewership is down four percent through two weeks (but it's still the third highest on record)
articles.summary: The second week of the 2026 NFL season attracted better viewership than the first week, relative to 2025.
articles.body:
The second week of the 2026 NFL season attracted better viewership than the first week, relative to 2025.

Via Austin Karp of Sports Business Journal , average viewership is down four percent in comparison to last year, through two weeks.

The games are averaging 19.9 million viewers over the first two weeks. The Week 2 games averaged 20.4 million.

Last week, the games averaged 19.5 million, a 13-percent drop over Week 1 from last year.

It's the third-highest average through two weeks in NFL history. The best years were 2015 and 2025.

Week 3 is headlined by Rams-Broncos on Sunday night, Ravens-Cowboys from Brazil in the late-afternoon window, and Eagles-Bears on Monday night.

Tonight's game features the Falcons at the Packers , the first of three straight prime-time games for 0-2 Atlanta .

articles.title: ‘Would Be the Worst Move,’ ‘How Does This Help Anything?’ — Giants Fans React to Team’s Rumored Interest in 2-Time Super Bowl Champion QB
articles.summary: With John Harbaugh as the head coach, the hype for the New York Giants was undeniable in the offseason. A potential playoff contender in the NFC, expectation...
articles.body:
With John Harbaugh as the head coach, the hype for the New York Giants was undeniable in the offseason. A potential playoff contender in the NFC, expectations were running high about their chances in the division as well.

A strong start in Week 1 provided further confirmation of their new-look roster. But an injury to Jaxson Dart might have derailed their entire campaign. Now they need an alternative, but one name being floated around has drawn utter disdain from the fan base.

Fans Aren't Happy With the Choices the New York Giants Can Make

A stellar game against the Dallas Cowboys in the season opener had fans extremely hopeful for the season. But against the Los Angeles Rams , a gruesome hit in the pocket caused an injury to Dart.

At the time, it looked like he might be out for some time but return later in the year. However, further reporting revealed the situation to be far worse than initially thought, with damage to his MCL, PCL, and meniscus ending his regular season.

With Harbaugh likely not wanting to punt on his first season with a new franchise, the Giants could look into alternatives to keep the team competitive. But one of the names making the rounds is veteran quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo .

Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post Sports reported, "The Jimmy G buzz is picking up. #Giants interest is real. @MikeGarafolo mentioned on @BigDayESPN that he thinks Jimmy G would be interested."

The two-time Super Bowl champion was a backup on the New England Patriots before finding the best stretch of his career with the San Francisco 49ers , even taking them to the Super Bowl, albeit in a losing effort.

However, the credit for the 49ers' success under him was largely attributed to head coach Kyle Shanahan's brilliance. Now, nearly two years after he last threw a pass in the NFL, fans are aghast at the idea of him being a legitimate choice from the Giants.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

"Would be one of the worst moves you can make," one fan claimed before doubling down and adding, "Would be the worst move easily."

"No thanks, he hasn't played in 2 years, he's 35 (34) years old, he's not worth it," one fan reasonably explained before offering an alternative, "How about Joe Milton ? He's on the Cowboys' practice squad. He has a similar profile of Dart mobility and a strong arm."

For one fan, though, the problem was from the Giants rather than the quarterback himself, as they claimed , "Jimmy isn't mobile! He will get killed behind that o-line."

Some fans joked that the decision to bring in Garoppolo could lead to superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers becoming frustrated with the situation and potentially demanding a trade from the team.

Other fans were aghast at the idea as well, even suggesting that the Giants then bring back Russell Wilson , who was booed by Giants fans during his final season with the team.

He wrote , "Really? A 35yo who was never that good and hasn't taken a snap in nearly 2 years? Why? Might as well unretire Russ at that point."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Another fan worried about the lack of mobility, exclaiming, "NOOOOOO, we don't need anymore statues."

However, most fans didn't want them to take an alternative route and stick with backup quarterback Jameis Winston instead. A rough showing against the Los Angeles Rams aside, his high-risk, high-reward style could benefit the team on some nights as well.

One fan claimed , "How does this help anything? They're either going to stay afloat with Jameis or just punt on the season (again). Jimmy G ain't Nick Foles ."

It remains to be seen if they actually pull the trigger to bring in Garoppolo. But as things currently stand, the move is being unanimously loathed by the fan base, so it might not be a smart way to appease them after the injury to Dart, who is currently ranked second on PFN's QB Impact Metric.

articles.summary: Follow along with the latest NFL news ahead of Week 3.
articles.body: Our second NFL week of the year is in the books, but unfortunately, it yielded a number of significant injuries, especially at the all-important quarterback position.After a hot start to the year, New York Giants QB Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury against the Los Angeles Rams Monday night, for which he will undergo season-ending knee surgery. Jameis Winston is set to start for the Giants for now, though head coach John Harbaugh did not rule out the potential for the team to trade for a veteran. The Chicago Bears are also expected to be without their starting quarterback for now after Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2. Head coach Ben Johnson dubbed him "week-to-week" on Monday, though the team did not yet officially rule him out for Week 3. That isn’t the end of their quarterback woes, however, as backup Tyson Bagent was placed in the concussion protocol earlier this week, which could force the Bears to start QB3 Case Keenum against the Philadelphia Eagles this week.Washington Commanders star Jayden Daniels also suffered a significant injury this week after dislocating his elbow for the second time since last season. He’s already been ruled out for Week 3 and is expected to miss additional time, though it’s unclear how much, as Daniels continues to gather opinions from specialists. Marcus Mariota will get the start in his absence.One team that is getting past a bad injury is the Falcons. After two weeks of disappointing outings from Cooper Rush, Atlanta announced on Monday that Michael Penix Jr. will start for the Falcons on Thursday against the Packers. A healthy Tua Tagovailoa is reportedly set to back him up.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 3.
